articles.title: US military disables tanker ship attempting to slip through Iran blockade on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary:
A U.S. military aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it tried to evade the naval blockade of all Iranian ports, which has been in effect since mid-July.

The Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer left Bandar Abbas, a major port city on Iran's southern coast, before the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) fired precision munitions at the ship's stern, destroying its propulsion.

A video released by the military shows a projectile hitting the back of the ship and causing an explosion. The civilian crew was unharmed in the strike, CENTCOM said.

So far, U.S. forces have redirected 158 compliant commercial vessels and disabled six that refused to comply.

TRUMP DARES IRAN TO BREACH US PORT BLOCKADE AS TEHRAN REPORTEDLY READIES 14 OIL TANKERS

President Donald Trump said Thursday, while celebrating Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, that victory in the Iran war would come "whenever I want it."

"We have victory at hand. It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said in a phone call to U.S. service members.

Trump also praised U.S. troops for their role in preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

TRUMP PAUSES TURKEY PARDON TO SALUTE US TROOPS GUARDING STRAIT OF HORMUZ: 'WATCH OVER AND PROTECT'

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you," he said.

Trump added that the U.S. has launched 150 missiles to intercept threats targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Asked whether Moscow and Beijing are providing Iran with intelligence to help it target U.S. military bases, Trump minimized the likelihood and said China was not heavily involved. He maintained that both countries are interested in helping the U.S. bring the war to a close.

Trump said that if the U.S. were to resume strikes, CENTCOM forces would "absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain," an underground complex near Iran's Natanz enrichment complex.

The likelihood of Iran agreeing to a deal proposed by the U.S. is low, Trump also told reporters.

articles.title: AI bionic eye breakthrough could help restore sight
articles.summary:
At a hospital in Spain, a 27-year-old man who lost his sight after a traumatic brain injury reported seeing flashes of light when researchers stimulated part of his brain. Those flashes were limited, but scientists have now used artificial intelligence to gain more control over the brain activity behind them.

The research could help make future artificial vision systems more reliable. Scientists are developing an AI bionic eye approach that learns how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation. Although the technology remains experimental, it could eventually help people who have lost their sight regain some degree of vision. 

So, how does this brain implant work, and what would it take to turn a few flashes of light into useful vision?

MOUTHPAD LETS YOUR TONGUE CONTROL A COMPUTER

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

When you look at something, your eyes send signals to your brain, which processes what you're seeing. But what happens when those signals can no longer reach the brain? For years, scientists have been developing electronic implants that attempt to restore some vision. 

Some stimulate the retina, the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. Others take a different approach by sending electrical signals directly to the brain. That's what makes this research interesting. Scientists are studying a device called a visual cortical prosthesis, sometimes described as a bionic eye. Despite the nickname, the implant goes into the brain rather than the eye.

It targets the visual cortex, the part of the brain responsible for processing visual information. When researchers stimulate this area with electricity, a person may experience flashes or spots of light known as phosphenes. These sensations can resemble glowing dots or simple shapes. However, getting the brain to produce consistent results has been a major challenge.

In 2024, researchers from UC Santa Barbara traveled to Spain as part of a collaborative study with ETH Zurich and Miguel Hernández University involving a 27-year-old man who had lost his sight after a traumatic brain injury. At IMED Elche Hospital, the man had received an experimental implant containing 96 electrodes placed in his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain implanted for six months before being removed.

During the study, researchers delivered small electrical currents through the electrodes. The man reported experiencing flashes of light and various shapes. That was encouraging, but the researchers wanted to go further. They needed to understand why certain electrical signals produced particular sensations and whether those responses could become more predictable.

FIRST-EVER GENE THERAPY FOR HEARING LOSS GETS FDA APPROVAL: 'GROUNDBREAKING'

This is where artificial intelligence helped the researchers make progress. Scientists trained a deep learning model to study how the man's brain responded to different electrical stimulation patterns. Instead of relying solely on the settings sent to the electrodes, the AI analyzed the actual brain activity those signals produced. It also considered what the brain was doing immediately before stimulation. 

That's important because brain activity can fluctuate over time, which can affect how someone responds to the same electrical signals.

Using this information, researchers identified stimulation patterns more likely to produce particular brain responses. When they tested those AI-designed patterns, the results improved. The researchers achieved greater accuracy in producing their intended patterns of brain activity while using less electrical current. They also discovered something important. 

The brain activity recorded after stimulation was a better predictor of what the man reported seeing than the electrical settings alone. In other words, knowing how the brain responded gave researchers a better indication of the man's visual experience.

Michael Beyeler, an associate professor at UC Santa Barbara who helped lead the research, explained the goal.

"Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around," he said.

That approach could help future implants adjust to changes in brain activity rather than depend on the same stimulation settings every time. The research was published in the journal Neuron.

It's an exciting possibility, but there's still a long road ahead. The man in this experiment experienced flashes and shapes of light. He did not regain normal eyesight, and researchers have yet to demonstrate that this AI approach can provide the functional vision someone would need to read or recognize faces. The experiment also involved only one participant. Scientists need additional research to determine how well the approach works in other people.

Still, the findings address a significant challenge. Researchers can stimulate the brain, but predicting exactly what someone will experience has been difficult. AI could help close that gap by learning how each person's brain responds and identifying better ways to deliver electrical signals. We've also covered a tiny retinal implant that helped people with advanced age-related macular degeneration regain some central vision. 

That device works with the retina and specialized glasses. The new research takes a different route by targeting the brain directly. It could eventually offer another option for people whose eyes or optic nerves can no longer send visual information effectively, provided their visual cortex can still respond to stimulation.

ROBOT PERFORMS 26 CATARACT SURGERIES WITH SURGEON CONTROL

Researchers still have several challenges to overcome before this technology could become a practical treatment. First, they need to demonstrate that the approach works safely and consistently in more people. Scientists must also determine whether the flashes and shapes produced by electrical stimulation can become useful visual information. Another challenge involves keeping the implant responsive as the brain changes. 

A stimulation pattern that works during one session may produce different results later.

The AI approach tested in this study offers a possible way to address that problem. However, researchers have yet to demonstrate a complete system that continuously adapts and delivers useful vision during everyday activities. For people dealing with vision loss today, technology already provides other forms of assistance. 

Our article on tech tools that make vision loss easier to manage at CyberGuy.com explores features that can help with everyday tasks. As for this new research, the next challenge involves turning more predictable brain responses into visual experiences that could help someone navigate the world.

The possibility of helping someone regain their sight through a brain implant is pretty remarkable. What I find especially interesting about this research is how AI could help scientists understand the way each person's brain responds to electrical signals. That could eventually make artificial vision more reliable. But there's still a big difference between seeing flashes of light and being able to recognize what's around you. I'd love to see this technology reach a point where someone who has lost their sight can recognize familiar objects or move around more independently. We're not there yet, and this was only one participant. Still, if researchers can turn these early results into useful vision, it could make an enormous difference in people's lives.

If scientists could someday restore even a small amount of your vision through a brain implant, would you consider the surgery, or would you wait until the technology could provide clearer sight? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Google Gemini may expose private emails to reviewers
articles.summary:
Think about everything sitting in your Gmail inbox right now. Maybe there's a conversation with your doctor, a recent bank statement or a personal message you never intended anyone else to read. Your Google Drive may hold years of private documents. You probably don't spend much time thinking about who might see that information beyond the people you share it with. But what happens when you connect those services to Google's Gemini AI assistant?

An independent researcher has raised concerns about how Gemini handles information retrieved from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The findings prompted questions about whether some private content could end up in conversations reviewed by humans.

We contacted Google, and the company confirmed that some information retrieved from connected Gmail and Drive accounts may be seen by human reviewers under certain circumstances. Google stressed that these connections are off by default. Here's what you should know before giving Gemini access to your personal information.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU

An independent researcher using the name thisisme6598 published findings on GitHub, raising questions about the way Gemini retrieves information from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The researcher tested Gemini using a personal Google Account with connected apps enabled. According to the published findings, Gemini sometimes retrieved information from emails or files during conversations without someone explicitly asking it to search Gmail or Drive. For example, the researcher described asking Gemini whether an internet service bill seemed too expensive. During some tests, Gemini reportedly retrieved billing information from Gmail, including payment amounts, account details and confirmation numbers.

In certain instances, the researcher reported that Gemini returned several sentences directly from an email and, in some tests, the entire email, including its headers. The researcher argues that this behavior creates a privacy concern because information retrieved into a Gemini conversation may become eligible for human review. However, the published findings do not establish that a human reviewer actually accessed the researcher's emails. Google told CyberGuy that the reported retrieval was standard behavior for someone who had voluntarily connected their apps. The company also emphasized that retrieved files remain visible only to the authenticated account holder and are not exposed publicly through this process.

Yes, under certain circumstances. Google's own Connected Apps privacy documentation confirms that trained human reviewers, including service providers, may review a subset of information processed through Gemini's connected apps. That information can include summaries or excerpts from relevant Gmail messages and Google Drive documents.

In some cases, Google acknowledges that reviewers may see a complete email or file if it is short or especially relevant to the request. Google also says human reviewers may access some Gmail inbox content when investigating abuse or harm or responding to submitted feedback.

The company uses these reviews to evaluate Gemini's responses and improve its services.

Simply using Gmail or Google Drive does not subject your private content to this review process. The concern involves information retrieved after someone voluntarily connects those services to consumer Gemini. Google says it does not train generative AI models directly on someone's entire Gmail inbox or Drive. However, relevant information processed during Gemini conversations may be used for model improvement, depending on account settings. Google specifically warns against connecting apps containing confidential information someone would be uncomfortable having a reviewer see.

We contacted Google directly to ask whether human reviewers could access Gmail messages or Drive files processed through the consumer Gemini app. We also asked whether the company had changed its privacy disclosures, notified existing customers and provided ways to prevent human review. A Google spokesperson told CyberGuy:

"Gmail and Google Drive’s core privacy protections remain unchanged, and your private emails and files are not reviewed by humans simply by using Gmail, Drive, or built-in Workspace features. Connecting those apps to the consumer Gemini app is off by default — it’s an optional way to get more personalized, time-saving answers across your Google apps when you want them. Users can disconnect their apps in Gemini settings at any time without losing access to Gemini’s core features."

Google also confirmed that when someone connects their apps to consumer Gemini with activity saving enabled, a small subset of conversations may undergo human review. Those conversations can contain relevant information retrieved from connected services. Before trained service providers review the material, Google says it separates the conversations from the associated Google Account and takes steps to reduce identifying information. The company also disputes the suggestion that the researcher's findings demonstrate public exposure of private files.

Another part of the controversy involves changes to Google's public privacy disclosures. In Oct. 2023, Google published a blog post about its approach to generative AI privacy. The company said that content from Gmail, Docs and Drive accessed through Bard's Workspace extensions would not be seen by human reviewers or used to train the Bard model.

On Oct. 16, 2026, Google added an update to that same blog post. The new language explains that Google has introduced additional optional features allowing people to connect Workspace information to other Google services. Google says that when someone enables these newer features, a subset of the information may be used to train generative AI models, depending on their settings. It may also undergo human review in limited circumstances. The researcher argues that the change represents a reversal of Google's earlier privacy commitment.

However, Google's original statement concerned Bard's Workspace extensions, while the updated disclosure addresses newer connected features. The available evidence does not establish that Google quietly changed the underlying handling of information in existing connections. We asked Google whether people who previously connected their accounts were notified about the updated disclosures or asked to provide additional consent. Google's response did not directly address those questions. Instead, the company emphasized that the newer connections are optional and can be disabled. That leaves an important question about how clearly Google communicates changes to its AI privacy practices, particularly as new features gain access to more personal information.

APPLE TIGHTENS MAC SECURITY AS AI AGENTS SEEK YOUR FILES

Google says it disconnects conversations from the associated Google Account before sending them to trained service providers for routine review. The company also takes steps to reduce personal information. However, removing account identifiers does not necessarily eliminate every sensitive detail contained in an email excerpt or document summary.

Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub explains that conversations reviewed by service providers may be retained for up to three years, even after someone deletes the corresponding activity from their Google Account.

Turning off Gemini's History setting, previously called Keep Activity, prevents future conversations from being used to train generative AI models unless someone submits feedback. However, Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes, including with help from human reviewers.

On Nov. 16, 2026, Google announced changes to its Gemini privacy controls. Under the previous policy, Google retained conversations for up to 72 hours when Keep Activity was turned off. Under the new policy, Google will retain conversations for approximately two months when History is turned off. The company is rolling out these changes globally over several weeks.

If you use Gemini, it's worth checking which accounts and services you've connected. You may find that you don't need every feature enabled. Here are some settings worth reviewing.

Google groups Gmail and Drive under Google Workspace in its connected-app settings. Here's how to check the connection on a computer.

If you see a different menu, look for Connected Apps in Gemini's settings. Google offers different connection controls depending on account eligibility and available features. You can reconnect supported services later if you decide to use them.

If you want to prevent future conversations from being used to train Google's generative AI models, review this setting.

Turning off History stops future chats from being used to train generative AI models unless you choose to submit feedback. Some connected apps, including Google Workspace, become unavailable. Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes. Depending on whether the latest privacy update has reached your account, conversations may be retained for up to 72 hours under the previous policy or approximately two months under the new policy.

WHAT YOUR INTERNET PROVIDER, WEBSITES AND ADVERTISERS SEE

Google is introducing a separate privacy control that lets you keep your Gemini conversation history while opting out of generative AI model training. If the new setting is available on your account, here's how to find it on a computer.

Google says future chats will no longer be used to train generative AI models unless you submit feedback. However, human review may still occur for other service improvements and safety purposes. If you want to prevent Gemini from retrieving information from Gmail and Drive, disconnect Google Workspace separately.

Disconnecting an app does not automatically delete information from earlier Gemini conversations. Google says Gemini may still use information from previously saved chats even after you disconnect the original app. That's why it's important to both disconnect the app and delete conversations containing sensitive information.

Remember that previously reviewed information may remain subject to Google's separate retention policies, even after you delete your activity.

Think carefully before giving an AI assistant access to confidential documents or personal communications. If you don't need Gemini to retrieve information from Gmail or Drive, leave those connections disabled. Also, remember that uploading a document directly into Gemini creates a separate privacy consideration.

Google says uploaded content may be used to improve its services when History, previously called Keep Activity, is enabled, potentially with help from human reviewers. Whether that content is used to train generative AI models also depends on your training settings and whether you submit feedback.

Google says the connected-app disclosures involved in this controversy apply to personal Google Accounts using consumer Gemini. Business, Enterprise and Education accounts covered by Google Workspace commercial terms have different privacy protections. According to Google's response to CyberGuy, customer data governed by those commercial terms is not reviewed by humans or used to train foundational AI models.

If you use Gemini through an employer or school, your organization's settings and agreements determine which features are available and how information is handled. The important point is that the consumer Gemini privacy rules discussed here should not automatically be applied to commercial Workspace accounts.

I can understand why someone would want Gemini to search their Gmail or find a document buried in Google Drive. We've all wasted time digging through old emails looking for something we need. Having an AI assistant do that work sounds pretty appealing. But I think Google has a responsibility to make the privacy implications much clearer before someone connects an account. Most people probably don't expect information pulled from their private emails to become part of a conversation that could eventually be reviewed by another human being. I appreciate that Google responded to our questions and explained the safeguards it uses. Still, I would have liked a more direct answer about whether existing customers were notified when the privacy disclosures changed. If you're giving an AI assistant access to years of personal information, you deserve to know exactly how that information might be handled. Personally, I'd leave Gmail and Drive disconnected unless I had a specific reason to use those features.

Would you trust an AI assistant with access to years of your private emails if you knew some of that information could be seen by human reviewers? Or has Google crossed a privacy line, even with your permission? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

articles.title: Supplements in the spotlight as longevity doctor shares his personal daily routine
articles.summary:
Nearly eight in 10 Americans take at least one dietary supplement for their health, according to a September 2026 Pew Research Center survey — yet clinicians warn that routine supplementation isn't always necessary or safe.

Dr. Kien Vuu, a Los Angeles-based physician specializing in longevity and author of the book "Thrive State," spoke to Fox News Digital about the role supplements play in overall health.

"Supplements are a signal," he told Fox News Digital during an event at Soft Bar + Cafe in Brooklyn, New York. "How we live life are signals. How we eat, how we sleep, how we move, how we connect with people, they're all signals to the body — and supplements can play a very important role."

DOCTOR'S 10 RULES FOR LIVING LONGER, CELEBRATING MORE BIRTHDAYS AND MAKING EXTRA YEARS COUNT

Certain supplements can support muscle growth, metabolism and cellular energy, but they work best when they're paired with "lifestyle choices and targeted support," the expert said.

Vuu, a partner with longevity and supplement brand Solaray, shared the supplements he takes on a daily basis.

Creatine, an amino acid-based compound, has become popular among fitness enthusiasts, as it has been shown to aid in boosting energy during exercise. The supplement is "really important" for muscle health and recovery, Vuu said.

COMMON GYM SUPPLEMENT COULD HELP FIGHT DEPRESSION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

The supplement has also demonstrated cognitive benefits, assisting with memory and processing speed, according to the National Institutes of Health.

Combining creatine with an MBP (milk basic protein) — a whey protein fraction studied for supporting bone formation and reducing bone breakdown — can support both muscle energy and bone health, according to Vuu.

NMN, short for nicotinamide mononucleotide, is a compound the body uses to make NAD+ — a vital coenzyme that helps cells convert food into energy and repair damaged DNA.

ANTI-AGING SUPPLEMENTS TAKEN BY MILLIONS MAY UNDERMINE CANCER TREATMENT, STUDY WARNS

As a basic step in his longevity routine, Vuu said he typically takes NMN to support cellular energy as natural NAD+ levels decline with age — though independent researchers note that clinical evidence in humans is still emerging.

Glutathione, a tripeptide antioxidant produced naturally in cells, helps the liver detoxify harmful compounds and protects cells from oxidative damage caused by pollution, stress and aging, according to UCLA Health.

In the body, the compound also plays a vital role in supporting immune and liver function, protecting red blood cells from oxidative damage and facilitating amino acid transport across cell membranes.

"When I travel or get super stressed, I like to use glutathione," Vuu said. "I find myself and my nervous system behaving a lot better."

Vuu also takes several staples aimed at filling common nutritional gaps, including vitamin D, magnesium, a multivitamin and fish oil for omega-3 fatty acids.

DR OZ REVEALS 3 FREE WAYS TO BOOST YOUR HEALTH — NO MEDICATION REQUIRED

"What I see very deficient in people these days is vitamin D," he said. "Even if they're out in the sun, our bodies are using so much vitamin D, fighting against some of the stresses we have in life, that it's really low."

Data from the National Institutes of Health shows that roughly one-third of U.S. adults are clinically deficient in vitamin D, and factors like sunscreen, winter sunlight angles, varying skin tones and higher body fat can limit how much the body produces.

"Supplementing with [vitamin D] improves their hormones, it improves their energy, it improves their sex life, improves their immune system," Vuu said — though clinicians note those benefits typically apply to people correcting a true deficiency rather than those whose levels are already normal.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The doctor said he also takes mitochondrial supplements such as ubiquinol — the active antioxidant form of CoQ10 — which supports cellular energy production and helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

While many people fall short on certain nutrients — or could benefit from targeted supplementation — it is possible to overdo it. Vuu said it's important to know your baseline health and to target your specific needs.

"If you're a person looking to supplement, go work with a physician first," he advised. "See where your labs are, see what symptoms you might be having, and then recognize what your goals are."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"The sweet spot is knowing what you need, knowing what the baseline is, and then taking the targeted [approach] to support you … You're not supposed to take everything, and it's going to be different for everyone."

Vuu added that supplements clearly play an important role in how the body functions, noting that "our cells are energetically listening to everything."

Supplements work best when paired with healthy lifestyle practices, including adequate sleep, regular exercise and social connections, he noted.

Connecting with people and maintaining a sense of community has been shown to be beneficial to health, Vuu said. Pairing a proven supplement like creatine with real-world connection and enjoyment, he said, creates the ultimate "health stack."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Beyond pills and powders, the expert suggested one final daily "supplement" for everyone: vitamin G — which stands for gratitude.

Recognizing life as a gift and feeling fortunate to be alive helps keep fear and anxiety at bay, he said.

"If you can feel gratitude, you're putting your nervous system in a state of calm, which actually improves symptoms and improves your health in the long term."

articles.title: Putin's grip on Crimea tested amid major blackout as Zelenskyy warns of looming Russian strike
articles.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin's control over Crimea faced renewed pressure Thursday as a massive blackout crippled the Russian-occupied peninsula, disrupting public transport and leaving people without heat, according to reports.

The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine.

Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post.

PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE

Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence suggested that Russia was preparing to target the country's energy infrastructure, logistics networks and essential services.

"Unfortunately, the Russians are already completing preparations for a new massive strike," Zelenskyy wrote on X Thursday following a coordination meeting. "According to intelligence, energy facilities and logistics infrastructure, as well as essential services facilities in cities and communities, will once again be the targets."

The Ukrainian leader also urged residents to remain vigilant, warning of renewed missile attacks.

"In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address Thursday, according to Reuters. "And in Russia, they should know that we will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike."

In Crimea, Russian-controlled electricity provider Sevastopolenergo said that Sevastopol had lost power, while electricity restrictions affected Simferopol, Kerch, Alushta and Yevpatoria, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

ZELENSKYY SAYS RUSSIA STRIKES HOMETOWN, CRITICIZES PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING

Streetcar services were also suspended in Yevpatoria and buses replaced trolleybuses on some routes in Simferopol. Parts of Kerch were also reportedly left without heating.

Russian-installed authorities had issued air raid alerts Thursday morning amid reports of explosions.

The blackout is the latest in a series of disruptions that have hit Crimea since late October, with Russian authorities blaming damage to power infrastructure.

The disruptions come amid mounting pressure on Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014 and has since used as a military and logistics hub for its operations against Ukraine.

The Kerch Strait Bridge, which connects the peninsula to mainland Russia, serves as a critical transportation link for Russian forces and has been targeted by Ukraine since Putin launched his invasion in 2022.

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

The bridge was built after the Russian annexation and opened in 2018, serving as a symbol of Moscow's control over the peninsula.

Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko also said seven people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital that damaged a shopping center and two other buildings, Reuters reported.

Zelenskyy also called for additional air defense assistance Thursday, emphasizing the need for interceptors for Patriot air defense systems and National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile Systems (NASAMS).

"I expect a report from Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry on the results of its communication with our partners regarding the supply of air defenses — interceptors for Patriots and NASAMS are the key priority," Zelenskyy wrote.

It was the second time this week Zelenskyy had warned of preparations for another major Russian attack, according to Reuters.

articles.title: Iran accuses Zelenskyy of 'false flag' Kuwait drone strike op to get Trump's attention
articles.summary:
A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team accused Ukraine on Thursday of orchestrating a deadly drone attack in Kuwait to prove its worth to President Donald Trump, as Tehran continued to deny responsibility.

And while Kuwaiti and Italian officials blamed Iran for the strike, which killed two Italian defense technicians and wounded two others, Iran’s embassy in Rome warned against "false flag" operations it said were aimed at widening the Persian Gulf conflict and now drawing Europe into the crisis.

Mohammad Marandi, who served as an adviser during talks with the U.S. in Pakistan and has been dubbed Iran's "English-language mouthpiece," claimed Ukrainian forces were operating across the Middle East, including in northern Iraq and Syria, also in remarks reported by the Fars News Agency, which is affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

IRAN TARGETS US AIR BASE IN KUWAIT AFTER US DEFENSIVE STRIKES AMID CRITICISM FROM GULF STATES

"It is widely believed in Iran that the attack on Kuwait was a false flag operation, likely carried out by the Ukrainian regime, because its operatives are now present across the region, including in northern Iraq and Syria. Ukraine aims to demonstrate its potential to Trump," Marandi said on X.

Fars also cited a security source who claimed Ukrainian operatives had deployed thousands of drones and other unmanned aircraft in several Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq's Kurdistan region, according to Iran International.

Kuwait's Defense Ministry said falling debris from the interception of Iranian drones struck a military facility Thursday, initially wounding four people. Two Italian nationals later died of their injuries.

A Kuwaiti national and a Pakistani national were also wounded and taken to a hospital for treatment. The ministry did not disclose the facility's precise location.

Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed that the two Italian nationals were employees of Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian subsidiary of German defense manufacturer Rheinmetall.

"An explosion caused by a drone attack ... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working," the ministry said in a statement.

The victims were identified as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, of Formia, Italy, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, of Rome, Italian news agency ANSA reported.

EUROPE ASSASSINATION SCHEME EMERGES AS IRAN DENIES DC 'DIRTY BOMB' PLOT AMID TRUMP WARNING

The men had been performing maintenance on detection antennas for the Skyguard air defense system.

Iran's embassy in Rome rejected allegations that Tehran was responsible for the attack, warning of alleged efforts to draw European countries into the Middle East conflict.

"The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran also draws the international community's attention to 'false flag' activities and operations aimed at expanding the scope of the conflict, linking disputes in other regions to the Persian Gulf crisis, drawing Europe into the crisis, and exacerbating the current critical situation, and calls on everyone to remain vigilant in this regard."

Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he had spoken with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and offered to cooperate in an investigation into the deadly incident.

"In calls with my Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts, expressed condolences over deaths of Italian citizens in Kuwait," Araghchi wrote. "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war.

"We stand ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident," he added.

TOP GULF OFFICIAL OFFERS GLIMMER OF HOPE ON TRUMP-IRAN NUCLEAR TALKS AS THREAT OF WAR HANGS OVER REGION

Kuwait, a key U.S. ally in the Persian Gulf, has repeatedly come under Iranian attack since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran on Feb. 28.

Ukraine has deployed drone specialists and interceptor drones to the Middle East to help defend against Iranian attacks, expanding its regional defense cooperation by sharing technology and military expertise developed during its war with Russia.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in March that Kyiv had sent interceptor drones and specialists to help protect U.S. military installations in Jordan at Washington's request.

Ukraine also announced that teams of military specialists had been deployed to Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia to help defend against Iranian drone attacks.

"Ukraine has the greatest experience in the world in countering attack drones," Zelenskyy said in March, adding that "without our experience, it will be very difficult for the Gulf region, the entire Middle East, and partners in Europe and America to build strong protection."

articles.title: UK shields fighter jets, contacts reservists in Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
articles.summary:
The United Kingdom is bolstering its military readiness amid growing threats from Russia, contacting former service members to assess its reserves as the Royal Air Force reportedly strengthens defenses against potential drone attacks.

Britain's Ministry of Defence has written to former service members to verify their contact information and military skills to ensure the country is prepared for a national emergency or potential conflict, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting confirmed Friday.

The outreach comes as the International Institute for Strategic Studies warned Thursday that suspected Russian-directed sabotage across Europe could trigger a "mass-casualty event."

NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL

The think tank found that sabotage incidents rose 16% in the year through September 2026, with Germany and Poland accounting for more than half of the cases. Researchers warned that a major attack could spark calls for retaliation and divide European governments.

"I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," Streeting told BBC Radio 4's "Today" program.

"You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," he said.

Streeting said the government needed updated records of its strategic reserve in case former service members were called upon to respond to a domestic disaster or overseas conflict.

He cited Russian incursions into Polish airspace, suspected Russian-sponsored sabotage across Europe and Iran-linked threats to British military bases.

Last week, a suspected Russian projectile landed in eastern Poland about 60 miles from a British-led military exercise. The incident happened the same day Britain's defense secretary and chief of the air staff visited troops.

INSIDE THE PENTAGON'S DOOMSDAY PLAN TO KEEP AMERICA FIGHTING IF GLOBAL WAR ERUPTS

"And so against that backdrop, against that threat environment, the government and the country has to be ready to face down those risks," Streeting said. "Because the more ready we are, the less likely we are to find ourselves in a conflict, in a war. That is my goal. That is the goal of this government."

The Ministry of Defence said in a news release it was contacting thousands of former military personnel this week as part of a drive to "strengthen the UK’s readiness and deliver on recommendations made in the Strategic Defence Review."

"Service Chiefs are writing to members of the Strategic Reserve, asking them to stay connected and update their details, providing Defence with a better understanding of the skills and experience it could draw upon if needed."

"In the coming months, Strategic Reservists will have the opportunity to volunteer for training and exercises, such as the UK’s participation in NATO’s flagship Steadfast Defender next spring."

The outreach marks the first time since the Cold War that Britain's defense ministry has contacted reservists on such a scale to encourage participation in military exercises, according to The Telegraph.

TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE

Meanwhile, Britain's domestic intelligence agency, MI5, and the defense ministry have reportedly warned British companies supplying military equipment to Ukraine that they could be targeted by Russian saboteurs.

The Royal Air Force is strengthening security at military bases, using hardened aircraft shelters and installing anti-drone netting to protect exposed fighter jets, according to The Times.

The measures follow Iranian threats against military bases in England that prompted tighter security and the relocation of U.S. military aircraft.

Suspected drone incursions over European airfields have also heightened concerns about Russian aggression.

"We take the security of our bases, equipment and personnel very seriously and are always adapting to counter any potential threats," a Ministry of Defence spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING

"This includes investing an additional £470 million to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection, surveillance and counter-drone capabilities.

"We have already invested £15 million in drone and counter-drone technology and introduced restricted airspace over 44 critical Defence sites."

The developments come as President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, signaling a shift in tone toward the Russian leader, whom he called a friend last week.

Trump said he made the request during a meeting with Putin in China last week, adding that he believed it could help secure a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

Trump's comments came a day after he hosted NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte in Florida. The two leaders issued a joint statement urging Russia not to expand its war in Ukraine.

"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Trump said on Truth Social.

articles.title: Ukrainian intelligence says North Korea paused missile deliveries to Russia amid friction over South Korea
articles.summary:
North Korea has temporarily halted shipments of ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia following diplomatic friction between the two allies over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian military intelligence said Thursday.

According to Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency, North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze on KN-23 ballistic missile and artillery deliveries last month after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko suggested Moscow would help de-escalate tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang, Reuters reported.

Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy toward South Korea, GUR said, though Reuters noted it could not independently verify the report or confirm public remarks from either official.

PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS

The reported pause also suspends Russian military flights over North Korea and stalls a Kremlin request to expand North Korea's troop deployment in Russia from roughly 8,500 to 50,000, according to the outlet.

Rudenko, who oversees Asian relations, said last month that Seoul had signaled interest in normalizing ties and resuming direct flights with Moscow once the Ukraine war ends.

Despite the reported freeze, North Korean troops remain active in Russia, with 11th Corps units serving in the Kursk region and a missile unit operating in Voronezh since mid-summer, GUR said. Russian President Vladimir Putin also hosted top Kim Jong Un aide Jo Yong Won at the Kremlin last week, where both men reportedly praised bilateral cooperation.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on social media Thursday that Moscow is "completing preparations for a new massive strike" on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services.

TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

Crews are already working to restore power in six regions after overnight Russian missile and drone strikes damaged an apartment building, a hospital and businesses, according to Zelenskyy, who also renewed appeals for U.S.-made Patriot air defense interceptors.

In Washington, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday that he urged Putin during talks in China to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."

U.S. envoy Jared Kushner, who is mediating talks with Steve Witkoff, said on the "MD Meets" podcast that Putin has "shown restraint" by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons, though negotiations remain deadlocked over Ukrainian territory.

Ukrainian forces also struck a Russian military airfield and an oil pumping facility overnight, while Russia claimed it intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: FlyDubai to resume Tel Aviv flights following attempted hijacking incident
articles.summary:
FlyDubai announced Thursday it will resume flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, next week, ending a suspension in place following an attempted hijacking incident in late September, according to media reports.

A source familiar with the matter told The Times of Israel that the airline is being allowed back into Israeli airspace "under new security arrangements."

The development comes after Transportation Minister Miri Regev decided this week that FlyDubai flights to Israel can resume pending clearance from Shin Bet, Mossad and Israel's National Security Council, the outlet reported.

A FlyDubai spokesperson told Reuters that the flights will begin again on Dec. 3. FlyDubai flights to Israel have been suspended since FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 on Sept. 30, when a co-pilot allegedly attacked his captain.

FLYDUBAI CO-PILOT ALLEGEDLY PLANNED TO CRASH ISRAEL-BOUND JET AT BEN GURION AIRPORT

That plane was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where it made a safe landing.

"Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian captain of FlyDubai Flight 1073, fought back after being stabbed in the cockpit," according to the Israel Foreign Ministry. "Despite being severely injured, he managed to unlock the cockpit door – allowing Israeli passengers and the Emirati crew to intervene and save all the passengers."

FLYDUBAI PILOT SHOWED WORLD 'THE HIGHEST FORM OF COURAGE,' INDIA'S PM SAYS

Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 reported that Hamam al-Hammami told investigators he intended to continue Flight FZ1073 toward Israel as though nothing was wrong, obtain the necessary clearances to approach Ben Gurion Airport and then crash the aircraft into a building or another plane at the airport.

UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said investigators determined that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act by attacking the captain with a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft.

Fox News Digital's Bradford Betz contributed to this report.

articles.title: Bangkok oil refinery explosion injures at least 9, Thailand company monitoring air quality
articles.summary:
At least nine people have been injured in an oil refinery explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, on Thursday, with three in critical condition.

The explosion occurred at a Bangchak Corporation-owned facility, the company confirmed in a statement posted to Facebook.

The company also claimed it was able to control and extinguish a large blaze caused by the explosion within 30 minutes of the blast.

EMERGENCY CREWS RESPONDING TO MASSIVE EXPLOSION AT NEW ORLEANS-AREA OIL REFINERY: SHERIFF

Additionally, it claimed monitoring showed no reduction in normal air quality.

"Since the incident occurred, the company has continuously monitored air quality in real time using automatic ambient air quality monitoring (AQM) stations, which the company has installed in the Phra Khanong, Bang Na, and Bang Nam Phueng areas to measure air quality around the refinery resulting from operations," the company wrote.

TWO INJURED AFTER EXPLOSION RIPS THROUGH CHEMICAL PLANT, SPARKING HAZMAT RESPONSE, SHELTER-IN-PLACE ORDER

"It was found that the air quality in the surrounding area of the refinery is within normal standards. Furthermore, at 5: 30 PM (17: 30 hrs.), the Pollution Control Department measured the air quality within a 3–4 km radius around the refinery—the same radial area—and confirmed that the measurement results are within normal standards," the statement added.

The company said it has also paused all production operations at the facility.

'PURE HELL' IN MOSCOW AS UKRAINIAN DRONES STRIKE MAJOR REFINERY SUPPLYING CAPITAL'S FUEL MARKET

Local authorities issued a mobile phone alert to nearby residents around 3 p.m. local time advising them to avoid the area.

Officials later told residents they could return home but advised those living within 5 kilometers (3 miles) of the facility to be wary of air pollution.

CALIFORNIA OFFICIALS WARN MASSIVE CHEMICAL TANK WILL LIKELY SPILL THOUSANDS OF GALLONS OR 'BLOW UP'

Thailand's Pollution Control Department also said it was monitoring air and water pollution levels in the area.

The country's energy minister, Akanat Promphan, said the fire likely started at one of the refinery units, which is hundreds of feet away from where oil is stored.

OFFICIALS SAY POSSIBLE CRACK IN UNSTABLE CHEMICAL TANK MAY RELIEVE PRESSURE AT AEROSPACE PLANT

"If we’re not a hundred percent certain that the oil storage is safe, we won’t allow them to resume operations," Promphan said.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Housefishing could fool you with AI real estate photos
articles.summary:
You find a beautiful house online. The driveway looks brand new, and the landscaping could be straight out of a home magazine. You get excited, schedule a showing and start thinking about where your furniture might go. Then you pull up to the address and wonder whether you're looking at the same house.

That's the growing concern behind housefishing, a term for real estate listings that use digitally altered or AI-generated photos to make properties look better than they actually are. A recent report highlighted complaints from homebuyers and renters who described misleading property pictures as "false advertising." With AI tools becoming more convincing, it's getting harder to know whether you're looking at a home's actual condition or a digital makeover. So how can you tell whether a listing photo shows the home you're actually getting, and what should you check before scheduling a tour?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

HIS HOME CHANGED HANDS FOR $5. COULD IT HAPPEN TO YOUR FAMILY?

Housefishing happens when property photos create an unrealistic impression of a home. AI can make an outdated property appear freshly renovated without anyone doing the actual work. For instance, two photos can show the same two-story house, but create very different impressions. 

The original photo can show a home with a dark asphalt driveway and large shrubs covering much of the front porch. But an AI-enhanced version can show a clean concrete driveway and a newly styled entrance.

This example shows how digital alterations can make a property appear to have undergone an expensive makeover. If those improvements exist only in the edited photo, someone visiting the property could be in for an unpleasant surprise.

Virtual staging has been around for years. Adding digital furniture to an empty living room can help buyers understand how they might use the space. AI simply makes those transformations easier and more realistic. But replacing a worn-out kitchen with an AI-generated renovation is another story. Laurent Cardinal, founder of real estate technology company Planpoint at planpoint.io/, believes agents need to be upfront about what they've changed. "The line is drawn where the intent is," Cardinal explains.

He supports using AI to show what a home could look like after renovations, provided agents clearly disclose the changes. His recommendation is straightforward: Show the original photo alongside the edited version so prospective buyers can compare them. However, digitally hiding property defects or replacing an unattractive view crosses that line. "That's cheating and it's hurtful to everyone in the market," Cardinal says. A misleading listing can waste someone's time and influence important financial decisions. For renters, the consequences can be especially serious if they send a deposit based on photos that fail to reflect the property.

You might think you'd recognize an AI-generated photo immediately. Maybe the furniture looks strange or a window seems out of place. Unfortunately, today's tools can produce convincing results. Sometimes the changes are subtle enough to escape a close look. Cardinal warns that even people familiar with AI-generated content can struggle to identify it. "But there's no silver bullet here, and anyone can get caught," he says.

Unusually perfect rooms can raise questions, especially when architectural details appear inconsistent between photos. However, traditional real estate photography can also be misleading. Wide-angle lenses make rooms appear larger, while carefully chosen lighting can minimize visible imperfections. AI creates an additional concern because it can alter the features of the property itself. That makes it increasingly difficult to judge a home's condition from listing photos alone.

FAKE VACATION RENTAL SITES USE LIVE CHAT TO STEAL YOUR DATA

The rules depend on where the property is located and which listing service an agent uses. California has already taken action. Under Assembly Bill 723, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026, real estate professionals must disclose covered digital alterations in advertisements for properties for sale. They must also provide access to the original, unaltered photos. The law covers changes made using traditional editing software or AI. Routine adjustments to lighting or color generally fall outside the requirements when they don't misrepresent the property. California has also approved Assembly Bill 2025. Starting Jan. 1, 2027, the state will require disclosures for digitally altered rental advertisements, with access to original photos when existing pictures have been changed.

Meanwhile, New York has warned agents about misleading AI property pictures. In November 2025, the New York Department of State reminded real estate professionals that advertisements must accurately represent properties for sale or rent. Agents who publish deceptive advertisements can face disciplinary action. Multiple listing services have their own restrictions. Stellar MLS, for example, requires disclosure of virtually staged photos and prohibits edits that conceal property defects or alter permanent features. There is currently no single nationwide law requiring every AI-edited real estate photo to carry a disclosure. Still, existing advertising laws and professional rules can apply when pictures mislead prospective buyers.

Interestingly, the same technology creating misleading property photos may also help identify them. Cardinal's company, Planpoint, connects listing photos to interactive floor plans. That allows prospective buyers to see how rooms fit together instead of relying on individual pictures that may be difficult to interpret. Its Planpoint Visit platform also offers AI photo detection. The technology checks newly uploaded property photos for signs of AI generation and displays a warning when it finds something suspicious. Cardinal says the company achieved a 98% success rate in its internal testing.

Before scheduling a showing or putting money down on a property, there are several ways to check whether the listing photos tell the whole story.

If a home looks suspiciously polished, ask the agent whether any pictures have been digitally altered. Request the original photos so you can compare them. Pay particular attention to kitchens and bathrooms, where expensive renovations can significantly affect a home's value. If an agent cannot explain what was changed, ask more questions before moving forward.

Cardinal recommends a simple way to verify a property's appearance. "The easiest way is to request a live video call with the agent or the owner," he says. Ask to see the areas you're most interested in, including anything that looks unusually perfect in the listing. A live walkthrough can reveal details that edited photos might hide. However, it cannot prove that the person showing the home has authority to rent or sell it.

Look carefully at the room dimensions and window locations. Then compare those details with the photos. Cardinal suggests asking, "Do the rooms and angles add up?" If a small bedroom appears enormous in a listing, ask whether the pictures were digitally altered. Remember that wide-angle photography can also exaggerate the apparent size of a room.

Search the property's address in Google Maps and look at the exterior using Street View. Compare the driveway and surrounding homes with what's shown in the listing. You might notice changes that deserve a closer look. However, Street View pictures can be outdated, so differences don't automatically mean an agent used AI.

Use Google Lens or another reverse-image search tool to check whether the same property pictures appear elsewhere online. You may find older listings showing the home before it was digitally enhanced. You could also discover that someone copied photos from another property to create a fraudulent rental advertisement. For help getting started, see our guide on how to reverse search an image on your phone.

Never rely solely on listing photos when making a financial commitment. If you're renting, independently verify the identity and authority of the landlord or agent before sending a deposit. For a home purchase, arrange an in-person showing and an independent inspection before committing to buy. A polished listing photo cannot tell you whether the property has hidden problems.

Those example of the two photos of the same house really show how far AI has come. The updated version looks fantastic, and I can see why someone would want to schedule a showing. But what happens when you arrive and discover that the beautiful driveway and landscaping don't actually exist? I think AI can be a great tool for helping buyers see a home's potential, especially if they're considering renovations. The problem starts when agents present those digital upgrades as the real thing. Buying a home is a major investment, and people deserve to know exactly what they're getting before they fall in love with a property online. I'd like to see more transparency from real estate agents, with original photos available alongside any AI-enhanced versions. There's nothing wrong with showing what a house could become, but buyers should never have to guess what it looks like today.

Would you walk away from a home if you discovered the agent had used AI to make it look better than it actually was, or would you consider that acceptable marketing? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Egypt detains driver suspected of causing Cairo fuel tanker crash and inferno that left 31 dead
articles.summary:
Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody.

The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared.

"It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock."

Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out."

STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION

Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames.

Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire.

They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. He then lost control of his car and veered far to the right while one of the fuel truck’s tires burst.

That caused the fuel tanker to hit the concrete wall of the highway and overturn, leading to the spill of fuel and the fire, according to the prosecutors' statement.

The stretch of the highway where the fuel tanker overturned is in Waraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area.

PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS

On Thursday, commuters and pedestrians stopped to examine the scene. Black scorch marks covered the metal railings of one of the highway exits, where pedestrians and hundreds of vehicles had been trapped Wednesday night.

A high-voltage electricity line also lay twisted on the ground amid the black soot, while piles of ash lined parts of the Ring Road, according to the AP.

For hours after the fire, the injured were still arriving at nearby hospitals as families gathered outside them in a mix of shock and grief. Authorities said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to the scene.

Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record, the AP reported.

In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a massive multi-car pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Thanksgiving on Ozempic: Clever tricks to survive the feast without offending the host
articles.summary:
With roughly 15% of Americans now reporting they have used a GLP-1 medication for weight loss, many Thanksgiving dinner plates may be a little less crowded this year.

Less "food noise" and a smaller appetite can make it tricky for people taking Ozempic, Wegovy or other glucagon-like peptide-1 drugs to navigate the etiquette of a traditionally large feast.

Patricia Araujo, a registered dietitian at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago, shared her practical tips for enjoying the holiday meal — without overdoing it or making your host feel slighted.

HOW SKIPPING BREAKFAST TO SAVE ROOM FOR DINNER SHOCKS YOUR BLOOD SUGAR AND METABOLISM

Handling topics around food and diet can be challenging for patients on a GLP-1, according to Araujo.

While people shouldn’t feel pressured to disclose anything about their personal or medical history, it can be helpful to think ahead of time about how much they want to share, she advised.

If guests question why you aren't eating a certain dish or urge you to take seconds, Araujo recommends having a polite response ready, such as, "That looks delicious. Thank you for offering. I've had enough," or simply, "I'm comfortably full right now."

THE 8 HEALTHIEST BEANS YOU SHOULD BE EATING MORE OFTEN, ACCORDING TO NUTRITION EXPERT

People don’t necessarily have to tell others that they’re taking medication, she noted.

"Sometimes just sharing that they're working on eating smaller portions, or they're making some dietary changes, but still acknowledging that the food is great and that they are happy to be able to share that meal together can be enough," Araujo said.

The dietitian recommends that people on a GLP-1 should get plenty of nutrient-dense foods, with an emphasis on protein, fiber, vitamins and minerals.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Protein is important because it helps us maintain muscle mass when we're taking a GLP-1 and losing weight," she told Fox News Digital.

At a Thanksgiving table, good sources of protein include roasted turkey without the skin, beans, chickpeas, lentils and tofu, Araujo said.

"Fiber is really important for digestive health and to keep things moving," she said. "Good sources of fiber are fruits, vegetables and whole grains. At Thanksgiving, that can be roasted vegetables, a leafy salad, maybe a baked sweet potato."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Because GLP-1 medications suppress appetite and can trigger side effects like nausea or constipation, rich, high-fat dishes are much harder on the stomach.

Araujo advises being cautious with fried foods, heavy casseroles and sugary desserts — anything loaded with butter, oils or heavy creams — and sticking to "smaller quantities or smaller portion sizes" if you do indulge.

People taking Ozempic or similar medications who have a decreased appetite shouldn’t feel obligated to load up their plates or eat to the point of discomfort, the dietitian said.

"Giving ourselves permission to eat smaller portions, not feeling pressured to have to finish everything on our plate, will be helpful during Thanksgiving," she told Fox News Digital.

To help manage portion sizes, Araujo recommends taking a look at what's available before putting food on the plate.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Another tip is to use a smaller plate, like a salad plate, if that's available," she suggested, noting that it’s best to eat slowly, take small bites and listen to "satiety cues."

"If you still have food left on the plate, I think asking for a to-go dish is always a good idea," Araujo added.

For those who are concerned that healthy foods might not be available on Thanksgiving, it’s wise to contact the host ahead of time.

"You can ask about food choices, or even offer to bring your own dish," Araujo said. "Use that as an opportunity to bring something that's nutrient-dense that you know you can eat and tolerate and still enjoy the gathering, but feel well."

When possible, she recommends putting a healthy spin on traditional Thanksgiving dishes. "For example, we can make stuffing healthier by swapping the white bread for a whole-grain, high-fiber bread and adding in some vegetables."

articles.title: Norse Atlantic airline suspends all flights, on brink of bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
articles.summary:
Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights Thursday as its board warned the company may imminently file for bankruptcy if it can't secure short-term financing.

"If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy," the company said in a statement.

The airline, which provides long-haul flights between the U.S. and Europe, said it had been discussing with investors a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution."

SHIPPING GIANT WARNS STRAIT OF HORMUZ CHAOS IS 'NEW NORMAL' AS TEHRAN SHIFTS 4M BARRELS

But, the company added, "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found."

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which contracts jets from Norse through a wet-lease program, shifted all United Kingdom flights to its own Boeing 777 planes, claiming Norse announced the suspension with no notice as PIA passengers were preparing to board.

Norse, amid rising fuel costs from the Iran war, began leasing out its Boeing 787 fleet to other airlines as it struggled to make a profit on trans-Atlantic flights. In July, IndiGo, India's largest carrier, announced it would conclude its own wet-lease program with Norse by the end of October.

Norse's stock price plummeted and closed down 85%. Most of its value has been wiped out since the start of the year and the stock is now trading at $0.010.

Jet fuel prices in Europe have more than doubled since March amid fallout from the Iran war and the restrictions on oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz, where up to 20% of the world's petroleum flowed before the onset of the war in February.

The price increases have forced other airlines, most notably budget carrier Spirit Airlines, to shut down as well.

DUFFY BLAMES BIDEN-BUTTIGIEG TEAM FOR SPIRIT AIRLINES COLLAPSE AFTER BLOCKED MERGER

"Long-haul, low-cost is most exposed to high fuel costs as demand is subject to a high level of price elasticity. So maybe not a surprise," aviation analyst James Halstead told Reuters.

Norse Atlantic did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Your holiday shopping data needs a cleanup before Black Friday
articles.summary:
Your phone buzzes: "USPS: Your package could not be delivered due to an incomplete address. Update your details within 12 hours." You did order something last week. Probably several things. So your thumb hovers over the link. That's the whole trick.

Black Friday lands on Nov. 27 this year, and the holiday delivery rush is already underway. That gives scammers plenty of opportunities to send fake delivery alerts that arrive when you're expecting a package.

Meanwhile, your shopping habits and personal details may be circulating through data brokers. Here's how that information can make scams more convincing and what you can do to clean it up before the holiday shopping rush gets even busier.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?

Every time you shop online, sign up for a discount or share your contact information, you may add to a growing collection of personal data. Some businesses use that information for their own marketing, while others share certain details with advertising partners or data brokers.

Here's where some of that information comes from:

As I've covered before, loyalty programs and store memberships can contribute to the information companies collect about you. Add the personal details available through people-search sites, and someone looking to target you may find more information than you'd expect. The FTC explains that people-search companies collect information from multiple sources and sell reports containing personal details, sometimes including relatives' names and addresses.

You can use the free exposure scanner we recommend at CyberGuy.com to check whether your personal information appears on publicly searchable websites. Keep in mind that a free scan cannot uncover every private data broker database. The results might surprise you.

WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES

A fake delivery text doesn't need to know exactly what you ordered. During the holidays, plenty of people are expecting packages, so a message about a delivery problem can seem believable. Scammers often send these messages to large numbers of phone numbers without knowing anything about the recipients. However, personal information obtained from public sources or data brokers can help make some scams more convincing.

Here's how that information could be misused:

The FTC reported that fake package delivery problems, often involving messages impersonating USPS, were the most commonly reported type of text scam in 2024. The problem extends beyond package deliveries. According to FTC testimony released in March 2026, Americans reported $15.9 billion in fraud losses during 2025 across all scam categories. A typical fake delivery message directs you to a convincing website and asks you to pay a small redelivery fee. That payment request is the trap. The scammer wants your credit card details and may also try to collect other sensitive information. Here's something important to remember: USPS does not charge a fee for redelivery. Its legitimate text tracking service also requires you to request tracking information first, and those tracking messages do not contain links.

Data removal takes time. Brokers process opt-out requests on different schedules, and personal information can reappear even after it has been removed. Starting now gives you a chance to identify exposed information and begin requesting removals before the busiest shopping days arrive.

There is one important distinction. Removing your information from data brokers can reduce your exposure over time, but it cannot guarantee that scam texts will stop or prevent scammers from contacting you this holiday season. That's why data cleanup should go hand in hand with safer shopping and delivery habits.

You can get started in about 15 minutes, although completing data removal requests and having companies process them can take much longer.

Look up your name on people-search websites such as Spokeo, Whitepages or BeenVerified. Check whether your home address, phone number or relatives' information appears. If you find information you want removed, look for the site's opt-out instructions.

Check the privacy settings on the websites and apps you use most frequently. Look for options to limit promotional emails, personalized advertising and sharing with marketing partners. You can also review saved shipping addresses and remove outdated entries you no longer need. Keep in mind that deleting a saved address may not erase information retained in previous order records.

If a message claims there's a delivery problem, open the retailer's or shipping company's official app or website yourself. Check the tracking number and delivery status there. Do not enter payment details through a link in an unsolicited message, even if it includes your name or address.

Instead of spending hours submitting individual opt-out forms, an automated data removal service can send removal requests to hundreds of data brokers, depending on the provider and plan you choose. Some services also submit recurring removal requests to help address information that reappears. While no service can erase every piece of information about you online, it can help reduce your exposure. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Talk with your parents and other relatives about fake delivery messages. Make sure everyone knows to verify unexpected payment requests through the carrier's official website or app. For USPS specifically, explain that it does not charge redelivery fees. A message demanding immediate payment to release a package should raise suspicion.

If you receive a suspicious delivery message, don't respond or click the link. You can forward scam texts to 7726 (SPAM) and use your phone's reporting feature. For messages impersonating USPS, you can also report them to spam@uspis.gov. If you already entered your credit card information on a suspicious website, contact your card issuer immediately. Ask about blocking the card, disputing fraudulent charges and monitoring your account for unauthorized activity. You can also report the incident at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

What concerns me most about these fake delivery texts is how easily they blend into our holiday routines. When you're ordering gifts and waiting for packages, a message about a delivery problem can catch you at exactly the wrong moment. I also think we need to pay more attention to how much personal information is floating around online. Taking a few minutes to search your name, review your shopping accounts and start removing exposed information is worthwhile. But remember, even if you clean up your data, scammers can still reach you. My advice is simple: Never let an unexpected text dictate how you check on a package. Open the official app or website yourself and verify what's actually happening before you share a single detail.
