He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them.

Khan added that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment.

Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh, over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

articles.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
articles.summary:
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army alleging that the pair were members of Hamas.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) claimed the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, were Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu.

MSF said it was “devastated” by the killings and denounced “a direct hit” on the organisation.

“Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military,” it wrote on X.

World Health Organisation chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus slammed the attack.

“Attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in #Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable,” he posted on X.

The IDF denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure. The Israeli military has regularly targeted health facilities in the besieged Palestinian enclave.

The latest attack comes amid a series of Israeli strikes targeting senior Hamas security officials in Gaza. On Wednesday, an Israeli air strike killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the group’s internal security service in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters at their apartment in Gaza City’s Beach refugee camp.

On November 24, Israeli air strikes killed at least three people in Gaza, including Adel Al-Helo, a worker with the UN Palestinian refugee agency (UNRWA), according to the agency and local health officials.

Al-Helo was working near a water well in Jabalia refugee camp when the strike hit. UNRWA said its staff were carrying out routine duties related to the well’s operations. The agency said three other people were wounded in the attack.

In a separate strike later that day, two people were killed when an Israeli air strike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, medics said.

articles.title: Driver, student injured as armed men open fire on students’ bus in Charsadda
articles.summary:
CHARSADDA: A driver and a student were injured when armed men allegedly opened fire on a coaster carrying students of Institute of Computer and Management Sciences (ICMS) College in the limits of Charsadda’s Nisatta police station late Friday night, police said.

According to Station House Officer (SHO) Nisatta Khan Zaib, two vehicles carrying around 70 students were returning from a recreational trip to Murree when the incident occurred.

The vehicles were travelling on GT Road after the motorway was closed and had reached the Nisatta area, he said.

SHO Zaib told Dawn that the firing stemmed from a dispute between two students during the trip. He said a case had been registered against two nominated suspects, while several people had been arrested in connection with the incident.

According to the coaster driver, who is the complainant in the case, a minor altercation had taken place between students during the trip. On their way back, the suspects, along with their accomplices, allegedly intercepted the vehicle and opened fire.

The firing left the driver and a student with bullet wounds. They were taken to hospital, where the driver was later referred to Peshawar for further treatment.

The complainant further alleged that the armed men had also tried to enter the vehicle but teachers standing near its door resisted them, preventing further harm to the students.

Meanwhile, District Police Officer Rafatullah Khan took notice of the incident and directed the police to arrest the nominated suspects without delay.

A special team, headed by Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Sardheri Bilal Haleem Khan and comprising SHO Zaib and other police officials, was formed to arrest the suspects.

According to a statement issued by Charsadda police, raids were being conducted at various locations to apprehend those involved. A case was registered under Sections 324, 427 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The president of the Private Colleges Association Charsadda, Sajjad Ali, and the president of the Council of Private Schools Association Charsadda, Mansoor Kausar Khan, condemned the firing.

In a joint statement, they demanded an impartial inquiry and the immediate arrest of all those involved. They warned that all educational institutions in the district would be closed in protest if the suspects were not arrested and justice was not ensured.

They also expressed concern over the safety of students and urged the police to take effective measures to prevent such incidents.

articles.title: US military says cyber systems secure after reports of Air Force hack
articles.summary:
The US military denied Friday any issues with its computer security following media reports that the Air Force’s cloud-based system was hacked, in what would be the latest high-profile breach of US digital infrastructure in recent weeks.

Asked whether the Air Force’s Cloud One platform had been hacked, the Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been breached.

Instead, a Defence Department official told AFP late Friday that “The Department of War’s systems are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world. We will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications.” “As a matter of policy and operations security, the Department of War does not comment on the status of our networks,” a Defence Department official said earlier on Friday.

NBC News, reported Friday citing an unnamed US official that the cloud platform had been breached and that an attack “could have exposed sensitive military information.” The breach was first reported by Reuters earlier Friday.

Federal News Network, which specialises in covering US federal agencies, also confirmed the breach, citing a “person familiar with the incident.” The contractors discovered the hack earlier in the year while doing maintenance on the system, Federal News said.

The reported attack is the latest in a string of major outages in US government and private-sector digital infrastructure.

In recent weeks the CIA and FBI were also reportedly subject to hacks.

Suppliers for major American financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard were also hit.

In other instances, such as a major Microsoft Outlook outage, a separate US air traffic control issue and a reported issue with a top-secret National Security Agency (NSA) network earlier this month, officials were at pains to blame the outages on maintenance or defects – not intrusions.

The attacks and outages are not limited to the United States.

The European Commission last week said it came under an AI-assisted cyberattack in October.

AFP was hit by a cyber attack on Thursday, forcing a major client-facing system to be taken offline.

articles.title: Pakistan Railways man booked for transporting dogs in train’s power van in Lahore
articles.summary:
LAHORE: During checking at Raiwind Railway Station, the railway police’ special branch staff recovered on Friday two dogs being transported illegally, without booking, in the Allama Iqbal Express (9-Up) power van.

According to officials, the train’s power plant operator, Mohammad Khan, allegedly charged Rs5,000 for transporting the dogs from Karachi, without booking them under the prescribed railway procedure.

The animals were reportedly to be handed over to a person at Kot Lakhpat Railway Station.

The police initiated legal proceedings against the operator, registering a case against him for violating railway regulations.

The dogs were subsequently booked, and a fine of Rs7,690 was deposited into the railway’s account, officials said.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: City Council approves Rs249m for Karachi's Burns Road Food Street
articles.summary:
KARACHI: The City Council on Friday approved a proposal to designate Burns Road Food Street as a pedestrian-only area and allocate an estimated Rs249.823 million for its renovation and development, reviving the initiative that had previously faced judicial intervention.

The move comes despite a February 2023 Sindh High Court directive to the local administration to end the evening food street operating on a portion of Burns Road and restore the road to vehicular traffic.

The latest approval raises questions about how the city administration intends to proceed with the project in view of the previous court order and the concerns of local residents and motorists.

The resolution was among 34 approved during the general session of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) City Council, held at the Council Hall under the chairmanship of Deputy Mayor Salman Abdullah Murad.

Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab and Metropolitan Commissioner Abrar Jafar also attended the session.

The Burns Road proposal started a debate in the house, with opposition members raising concerns over restricting vehicular movement and the difficulties the pedestrian-only arrangement could create for residents and businesses in the surrounding area.

Defending the initiative, Mayor Wahab said: “Burns Road is a historical heritage site. We are going to restore our historical heritage. We will improve Burns Road and all the adjoining streets and provide the citizens with the best facilities,” the mayor said.

The meeting also witnessed heated exchanges over the Nehr-i-Khayyam project.

Opposition Leader Saifuddin Advocate expressed reservations, arguing that the waterway served as a drainage channel for rainwater from the surrounding areas.

Another resolution, however, seeking separation of sewage from the canal and installation of parallel sewerage lines was unanimously approved to prevent pollution and restore the waterway as a recreational facility.

Council member of Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) Najmi Alam supported the initiative, saying the project envisaged treating wastewater and introducing boating facilities.

Responding to criticism, Mayor Wahab said Nehr-i-Khayyam was not the project of any single political party or government but an initiative intended to benefit Karachi’s residents.

He also said opponents had approached the courts over the project and maintained that the people of Karachi should have a say in how their city was managed.

The mayor defended his administration’s performance, inviting scrutiny of its expenditure and assuring council members that development projects would be subject to accountability.

He said third-party consultant verification had been made mandatory for all major projects for the first time.

Earlier, Opposition Leader Saifuddin Advocate raised concerns over the powers and resources available to union committee chairmen, claiming that the withdrawal of sanitation staff and administrative authority had weakened their ability to address public complaints.

He also questioned the performance of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation, citing repeated shutdowns at the Dhabeji pumping station and prolonged water shortages in several localities.

Among other major decisions, the council approved a Rs100 million annual grant to Karachi Metropolitan University to make the Quaid-i-Awam Block at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital operational.

It also approved an increase in long-pending allowances for KMC hospital nurses, revival of the Nursing College at Karachi Institute of Heart Diseases, and payment of Rs425 million in reconciled outstanding dues to K-Electric.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Tandoor owners threaten to stop selling roti from Dec 4 in Punjab
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Protesting over the increasing actions of the Punjab Enforcement & Regulatory Authority (Pera) Force over using subsidised wheat flour, tandoor owners have announced that they will stop selling rotis from Dec 4 across the city.

The announcement came after the Pera Force started sealing tandoor shops, having wheat flour bags procured on subsidised rates, claiming that tandoors were not authorised to procure subsidised flour. Following the action, tandoor owners had staged a protest demonstration at the DC Office a couple of days ago to demand an end to Pera actions and provide wheat flour on subsidised rates so they could sell rotis at notified rates.

“All was going well and we were selling sada roti for Rs17 following the provision of a 10kg flour bag at Rs1,100. But all of a sudden, the government increased and fixed the 10kg flour bag price at Rs1,275. The Pera Force also started sealing tandoors, having flour bags purchased on subsidised rate. So far, eight tandoors have been sealed,” Mutahidda Nan Roti Association President Aftab Gill told Dawn on Friday.

“While the LPG prices are already on the higher side and gas loadshedding is also ongoing, we are unable to sell roti for Rs17. Therefore, we have decided to better stop baking flatbread with effect from Dec 4,” he argued.

He said the Dec 4 deadline was given just to give the government time to think and consider the demands of the association, comprising as many as 15,000 tandoors across Lahore city district.

“We need 15,000 flour bags (80kg each) daily for all tandoors. If the government gives us the bags on subsidised rates, we can sell roti for Rs17, failing which, we will have no option but to stop baking flatbread,” he warned.

Meanwhile, the association, through a written application to the Lahore DC, has also sought notifying the roti rate at Rs30, keeping in view the increasing rates of wheat flour.

The DC was not available for comments.

COMMISSIONER: Lahore Commissioner Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan on Friday visited several sites in the Walled City to review the progress of ongoing development and conservation projects, including work at Mori Gate, Taxali Gate, Sheranwala Gate and Pani Wala Talab.

During the visit, the commissioner reviewed sewerage, restoration and construction work being carried out under various development schemes.

Officials and engineers from the Walled City of Lahore Authority, Communication and Works Department, Nespak and project monitoring teams briefed him on the progress of the projects.

Mr Awan inspected the outer drain at Mori Gate and reviewed the preservation and restoration of historic buildings.

He also visited Government Victoria Girls Higher Secondary School inside Mori Gate, where he was briefed on the proposed conservation work. He also reviewed progress on the underground parking and market project at the Taxali Gate.

The commissioner was further briefed on the conservation and upgradation plans for Pani Wala Talab being undertaken by the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa).

Officials said the reservoir, established in 1883 and supported by 518 pillars, continued to serve as an important source of water supply for the city.

During the visit, Mr Awan also reviewed larva surveillance activities being carried out by anti-dengue teams in the Walled City. He interacted with residents and distributed pamphlets as part of the dengue awareness campaign.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Hope for more survivors revives after man pulled alive from rubble
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Amid piles of rubble, the roar of heavy machinery and the constant movement of rescue workers, several people gathered at the site of the building collapse in Block 4 of Karachi Administration Housing Society, anxiously hoping that their loved ones may still be found alive beneath the debris.

Rescue workers and volunteers are engaged in clearing the rubble and trying to reach those who may be trapped, while every passing moment adds to the distress and uncertainty of the affected families.

Whenever the heavy machinery is halted to allow rescue workers to enter the debris and look for signs of life or recover bodies, the anxiety of relatives at the site intensifies.

Some try desperately to move closer to the rubble, hoping for news of their loved ones. One family is searching for a missing brother, another for a son, while others wait anxiously for any information about their relatives.

Families of those trapped in the debris express dissatisfaction with pace of search; DC says operation is continuing uninterrupted

For these families, the operation is not merely a rescue effort but an ordeal in which hope and fear remain suspended between life and death.

Their hopes revived when a man buried under the rubble was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassanul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that after tracing the man trapped in a pocket, rescuers provided him with oxygen and, following a delicate operation lasting two to three hours, brought him out alive.

“Initially, he was in trauma, but after receiving first aid, his condition is now stable. He also recorded a video message in which he told the rescue team that he, his ustad [master], and a helper were busy working when the building collapsed and fell on them, but the other two persons could not be traced,” the spokesperson added.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude over the man’s survival after being trapped under the rubble for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”.

According to a statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to expedite the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

He also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure that the survivor received the best possible medical treatment.

10 still trapped

The Rescue 1122 spokesperson said that 10 people were still missing, as per reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building. He added that a search operation was ongoing to locate any other survivors from the debris.

While families of those missing remained dissatisfied with the pace of the search operation, Deputy Commissioner East Kashif Nabi Khuhro said the rescue operation was continuing without interruption.

Talking to newsmen, he denied that the pace of the rescue operation was “slow”. However, he pointed out that the collapsed building was “situated in congested, narrow streets, and it was difficult to move heavy machinery there”.

Imtiaz Ali also contributed to this report

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Love at scale
articles.summary:
RECENTLY, the second Global Ministerial Conference to End Violence Against Children was held in Manila. Ministers and government officials from all over the world came together to assert their commitment to protecting children, and to make concrete pledges to work towards in the next two years.

Among the plenary speakers was Dr Nadine Burke Harris, a paediatrician and former surgeon general of the state of California. Her work has been dedicated to making the link between adverse childhood experiences (ACES) — including neglect, violence, poverty and abuse — and long-term impact on adults.

Prolonged exposure to toxic stress has a biological response, with negative impacts on health and life potential. These can range from heart disease to obesity and substance misuse, to impact on brain development, with difficulties in learning or self-regulating.

On the other hand, the experience of loving and nurturing support can have a buffering effect for children, tempering the effects of their difficult realities. Especially if support is offered early, it can transform a future. That’s why, she argued before global delegations, when it comes to child protection, “infrastructure is love at scale.”

The experience of loving and nurturing support can have a buffering effect for children, tempering the effects of difficult realities.

What this means is that if done right, child protection systems would represent a continuum of care. Right from prevention to recognising the signs for when an intervention is needed, to appropriate case management, response and essential follow-up. Allocating enough resources to have effective referral pathways, trained personnel and data management — that would be an act of love by those with power over budgets.

In Pakistan, the scale of challenges is both vast and daunting. Where do we even start? From children visibly exposed to insecurity on the streets, to those in distant villages quietly experiencing the impacts of climate change on their households, it seems impossible to address all the structural factors behind violence.

Chronic economic stress increases the risk of violence within households, as well as of child labour that sends children out without guardrails. Then there is the plethora of departments that need stitching together — health, education, social welfare, law enforcement. Each one has a role that needs to be clearly understood, so that the doctor or teacher seeing a child in suffering knows how to recognise physical and psychological injury, and who should be handling it next.

The minister for human rights, speaking before the world, shared the launch of a National Action Plan and strategy for child protection. It is apt that the oversight of this strategy falls under human rights, which must be guaranteed to every child regardless of geography, ethnic or religious identity.

However, what is crucial at this point is to acknowledge the need for inter-ministerial and inter-departmental cooperation, for which the MoHR can act as a conduit. The ministry of education and professional training, for instance, has a key role in ensuring that schools are both safe and enabling, and an important point of connection with children and families.

It also has a key role in creating a culture of care for children, with educators beginning to disrupt the normalisation of corporal punishment and violence as a tool for discipline. In that sense, the conference was a unique opportunity to really learn from global experiences of navigating bureaucracy and politics, to get to what matters.

All this being said, there are limitations to scale. Social services even in the most “developed” contexts can get it wrong, when mechanically applying standards to children or families under stress.

Love at scale cannot mean that children are not seen for their individual circumstances, or are separated from families without working through challenges. If anything, love will be made up of the countless tiny acts and steps taken by the frontline workers who come into contact with vulnerable children, the conversations they are able to have, the kindness they show in response.

Again, teachers can represent essential allies in a protective ecosystem. Not only do they know individuals, communities and their challenges, but can be reliable sources of support that children see every day. Within a compassionate classroom, they can create trust, joy, and hope for a positive future.

The theme for World Children’s Day this year was “My day, my rights, my future.” This is not the first time we have heard words like this; perhaps that is why it is a time of great reckoning in the sphere of human rights and development, with a tragic deficit of resources and trust in the sector. However, what finally needs to be understood is that civil society alone cannot stop all the gaps, even while being able to offer the state both technical support and insights from community work.

Manila was an illustration of how it is possible to make space for high-level official dialogue as well as learning from academic research, and ground-level implementation experience incorporating children’s voices. If this time we truly want love at scale, it will take all of us, working to cover the crevices that children can fall through.

The writer is CEO of Cities for Children, an organisation that works to protect childhood.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Courts yet to settle if men can be prosecuted over ‘marital rape’: report
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan removed the marital rape exception from its criminal law two decades ago, but the courts have yet to settle whether a husband can be prosecuted for raping his wife, according to a new report by the South Asian Movement for Accessing Justice (SAMAJ), a coalition of 26 organisations convened by Equality Now.

The report, Challenging the Marital Rape Exception in South Asia, led and authored by lawyer Sahar Bandial, reviewed the law in eight countries.

It noted that the Protection of Women (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2006 redefined rape under Section 375 of the Pakistan Penal Code without reference to marital status, so marital rape can in principle attract the same penalty as any other rape. Yet no reported superior court judgement has confirmed this.

Cases described in the media as marital rape convictions have mostly been brought under Section 377, which covers “unnatural offences”.

Sherry urges action against child marriages; says one in six women in Pakistan was married as a child

In August 2026, a special court in Lahore sentenced a man to ten years under Section 376 for raping his wife — a clear marital rape conviction, the report says, though only at trial level.

By contrast, a 2025 Lahore High Court ruling held that forced sex within an ongoing marriage was not rape, effectively reading the exception back into the law.

In November 2026, the same court dismissed a petition seeking directions for legislation on marital rape. Domestic violence laws offer only civil remedies.

Regionally, the Maldives is the only country to fully criminalise marital rape on par with other rape, following a 2021 amendment. Nepal and Bhutan criminalise it with far lighter penalties. India and Sri Lanka recognise it only where spouses are separated; Bangladesh exempts husbands whose wives are over 13, and Afghanistan has no applicable law.

The World Health Organisation estimates cited in the report put lifetime intimate partner violence in Pakistan at 24.8pc, below Afghanistan (50.9pc), Bangladesh (48.9pc) and India (29.9pc), though the figures do not isolate marital rape.

The report urges legislators to make consent within marriage explicit in law.

Child marriages

Meanwhile, in a statement on the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, Senator Sherry Rehman called for stronger legal protections, effective enforcement and sustained efforts to address the social and economic factors driving child marriages.

The PPP leader stressed that the practice deprived girls of their childhood, education, dignity and fundamental human rights.

“One in six women in Pakistan was married as a child. Pakistan ranks sixth globally among countries with the highest number of child marriages, while more than 19 million women and girls in the country were married before the age of 18. Nearly 4.8m girls were married before the age of 15.

“Globally, around 650m women and girls have been married in childhood. These are not just statistics; they represent millions of lives shaped by lost opportunities, interrupted education and diminished choices,” she said in a statement issued here.

She noted that child marriages had become particularly prevalent in flood-affected areas, where families facing displacement, poverty, loss of livelihoods and insecurity increasingly viewed early marriage as a survival mechanism.

“When disasters push families deeper into poverty and insecurity, girls are often the first to bear the cost. Marriage cannot be a coping mechanism for economic hardship, displacement or climate-induced vulnerability.

“It further exposes girls to risks and deprives them of the opportunity to rebuild their lives through education and empowerment,” she said.

Senator Rehman said the legislation had strengthened the legal framework for accountability and protection, but laws alone could not deliver justice without effective implementation, institutional commitment and public awareness.

“Every girl has the right to learn, to make decisions about her own future, to grow up without fear and to live a safe and dignified life. We cannot protect our girls through legislation alone unless we confront the inequalities and economic pressures that make child marriage possible,” she said.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: PM calls for stronger Pak-Oman ties
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has called for further strengthening Pakistan’s bilateral cooperation with Oman, particularly in trade, investment, energy and defence.

During a meeting with the Omani ambassador at the Prime Minister’s House, the prime minister highlighted the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Oman, rooted in shared history, faith and culture.

According to a Prime Minister’s Office news release, PM Shehbaz stressed the importance of translating the positive momentum in bilateral relations into tangible results through increased economic engagement and institutional cooperation.

The two sides also discussed recent regional and global developments. The prime minister emphasised the importance of maintaining peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy.

The Omani ambassador than­ked the prime minister for receiving him, conveyed the greetings of the Omani leadership and reaffirmed his country’s commitment to further strengthening its close relations with Pakistan.

PCSIR role in exports

Separately, PM Shehbaz on Fri­day directed the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Indus­trial Research to enhance its research capabilities and contribute more effectively to industrial development, export growth and the promotion of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

Chairing a meeting on matters related to the PCSIR, the prime minister said the institution could play a significant role in helping Pakistani products compete in international markets.

He directed all PCSIR laboratories to obtain accreditation in accordance with international standards to facilitate internationally-recognised certification and validation of Pakistani export products.

The prime minister also called for stronger cooperation between the PCSIR and the National Vocational and Technical Train­ing Commission (NAVTTC) to improve industrial and technical training opportunities for young people. He sought the report of the third-party validation conducted on the institution.

The prime minister constituted a committee to review the PCSIR’s mandate, performance and future role. The committee will examine the institution’s original objectives, legal responsibilities, achievements and untapped potential, and recommend measures to improve its contribution to the national economy, industrial development and exports.

The meeting was informed that the PCSIR operates 10 research laboratories and units across the country, along with seven technical training institutes, while 12 additional laboratories are nearing completion.

The institution provides industries with modern technologies, research facilities and affordable technical solutions aimed at improving productivity and product quality.

Officials informed the meeting that the PCSIR had provided technical training to more than 12,000 young people. Its research and development activities cover a wide range of sectors, including food, agriculture, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, textiles, leather, minerals, engineering and energy.

The briefing further highlighted that PCSIR laboratories provide domestic industries and exporters with facilities for product testing, quality verification and calibration of technical instruments.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: AJK PM extends olive branch to protesters in Rawalakot
articles.summary:
• Gillani says govt ready to discuss all demands within constitutional, legal framework
• Urges protesters to dissociate themselves from armed groups
• Speaker calls for elections to fill seven vacant assembly seats

MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani on Friday offered to discuss the demands of protesters in Rawalakot within the constitutional and legal framework, but urged those involved in the unrest to dissociate themselves from armed groups.

Addressing a PML-N public meeting at Lal Chowk, the prime minister said the AJK government was prepared to take every possible measure, in the light of a recent resolution of the assembly, to restore peace and stability in the region.

“We are ready to discuss every demand that falls within the ambit of the Constitution and law. Disa­ssociate yourselves from armed groups; dialogue can only take place within the constitutional and legal framework,” he said.

Mr Gillani said some people publicly distanced themselves from armed groups but continued to provide them space, which was detrimental to efforts to restore peace.

Referring to some of the protesters’ demands, the prime minister said the government was planning to establish catheterisation laboratories (cath labs) and stroke centres in different parts of AJK. The government was also pursuing road improvement projects and the Kashmir Express electric bus service, besides planning employment and self-employment opportunities for young people, he said.

“Our aim is not to make a flurry of announcements but to translate plans into practical measures and deliver results,” he added.

100-day action plan

Referring to the 100-day action plan, Mr Gillani said his government had drawn up a strategy extending to five years, adding that decisions concerning the state’s future and prosperity required careful planning.

He said four governments had changed during the previous tenure, disrupting development activities and affecting

the resolution of public problems. His administration would focus on ending political uncertainty and improving governance, he added.

The prime minister said the plan covered healthcare, education, employment, tourism, transport, digital governance and urban development, with several initiatives to be implemented during the first 100 days and others continuing beyond that period.

He said recruitment in government departments would be carried out thr­ough third-party agencies on merit, while interest-free loans would be offered to young people to encourage entrepreneurship and self-employment. Schola­rships at leading universities would also be provided to deserving students.

Tourism promotion, public-private partnerships for government rest houses and facilities for local businesses would help generate investment and employment, he said. Digitalisation of government services through the AJK One Portal was intended to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and spare citizens repeated visits to public offices.

Mr Gillani said the government would also introduce housing loans for deserving people, improve sanitation in all 10 district headquarters and undertake beautification projects in Muzaffarabad.

He said the coming 100 days would provide an opportunity for people to assess the government’s performance following the Nov 18 visit to Muzaffarabad by PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.

“Building roads and public infrastructure alone is not enough; the state also needs to address its underlying problems. Society must restore moral values and mutual respect. Differences of opinion do not justify humiliating one another,” he said.

Call for dialogue

Earlier, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq said the government had assumed office to serve the people and promote development and public welfare.

He said the Kashmir freedom movement remained the party’s fundamental objective and that it would defend Pakistan’s interests in AJK while preserving the distinct identity of Jammu and Kashmir.

Referring to a recently adopted Assembly resolution, he said it reflected the common position of the people of AJK, the PML-N and all political parties represented in the legislature.

Mr Farooq said the people of Poonch should regain their right to representation through elections on the seven Assembly seats that remained unfilled, thereby completing the strength of the legislature.

Energy and Water Resources Minister Saqib Majeed Raja said unrest and uncertainty in AJK since 2023 had affected the region’s administrative system, economy and everyday life.

He urged society to assess what it had gained and lost during the past three years, saying the support and solidarity extended to Kashmiris by the people of Pakistan were a valuable asset that should not be squandered amid political differences.

He said lasting solutions to public grievances lay in dialogue, democratic processes and effective performance by elected representatives rather than protests, confrontation and vandalism.

People should give their elected representatives an opportunity to resolve their problems, he said, adding that voters had the power to reject them in the next elections if they failed to meet public expectations.

Several other PML-N leaders also spoke on the occasion.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Seven terrorists killed in Bannu operation
articles.summary:
BANNU/SWABI: Security forces killed seven terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Shoikhel area of Bakakhel tehsil in Bannu district, official sources said on Friday.

They said that security forces targeted a suspected hideout with a drone strike following information about the presence of around 10 militants inside a house.

The sources claimed that seven suspected militants were killed in the operation. However, details about the remaining individuals have not yet been made public.

The security situation in Bannu has remained a matter of concern over the past several months. Areas, including Bakakhel, Miryan, Janikhel and Wazir subdivision have witnessed attacks on police and security personnel, bomb blasts and reported militant movements, creating a sense of insecurity among residents.

In recent days, security forces, police and the Counter-Terrorism Department have intensified IBOs and search activities in different parts of the district.

On Nov 25, a joint operation in the Garerha Shah Jahan, Kingar and adjoining villages of Bannu reportedly resulted in the killing of three suspected militants, while several suspected facilitators were taken into custody.

Earlier, on Nov 6, a suspected militant was killed during an operation in the mountainous area of Rocha in Bakakhel. Security sources said operations were continuing in different areas to target militant networks, suspected hideouts and their alleged facilitators.

Meanwhile, an official of the Ababeel Rider Squad was injured when two unidentified motorcyclists opened fire on them in Swabi on Friday, local sources said.

They said that the incident took place near a hospital on Swabi-Mardan Road. The injured, identified as Saqib Khan, was immediately taken to Bacha Khan Teaching Hospital.

However, a police spokesperson said that Saqib was injured when the pistol of his colleague accidentally went off.

Separately, a young man was killed over a monetary dispute in the Maneri Bala area of Swabi.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

articles.title: Pakistan Shaheens cruise into Asia Cup Rising Stars final with five-wicket win over Bangladesh ‘A’
articles.summary:
Pakistan Shaheens produced a composed five-wicket victory over Bangladesh ‘A’ in the second semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Friday, chasing down a target of 233 with 28 balls to spare to book their place in Sunday’s final against Sri Lanka ‘A’.

The defending champions reached 233-5 in 45.2 overs after Bangladesh ‘A’ had posted 232-8 in their 50 overs. Hasan Nawaz, who made 62 and claimed two wickets, was named player of the match.

The chase was shaped by a measured third-wicket partnership between Hasan and Shahzaib Khan, who steadied the innings after Pakistan had lost both openers inside the first five overs. Shahzaib made 50 from 85 deliveries, while Hasan’s 91-ball 62 included three fours and three sixes.

Pakistan’s start had been unsettled by Bangladesh seamer Ripon Mondol, who removed the openers early and left the Shaheens needing to rebuild.

Hasan countered with calculated aggression, including a six off Iqbal Hossain Emon that eased the early pressure, while Shahzaib concentrated on occupying the crease and rotating the strike.

The pair took the total to 128 before Hasan was trapped leg-before by Md Rubel in the 31st over. Shahzaib continued to anchor the innings, bringing up his half-century before falling in the 35th over to an excellent diving catch by substitute fielder Rizwan at midwicket off Rakibul Hasan.

With the innings requiring fresh impetus, captain Abdul Samad and Farhan Yousaf took charge. Samad struck 44 from 33 balls, adding momentum with forceful strokes through the leg side, while Farhan remained unbeaten on 46 from 39 deliveries.

Their partnership carried Pakistan through a testing middle phase, with the required rate kept within reach despite a couple of quiet overs and a near run-out involving Farhan.

Samad’s dismissal, with the target in sight, did little to derail the chase. Farhan kept his composure, declining unnecessary risks and ensuring the innings moved forward. Pakistan crossed the line in 45.2 overs, with Rohail Nazir alongside Farhan when the winning run was completed.

Earlier, Bangladesh ‘A’ had been lifted by a superb unbeaten 103 from Shahadat Hossain, whose innings rescued a side that had struggled for momentum in the opening half.

He faced 118 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, and shared a 95-run third-wicket partnership with Mahidul Islam Ankon to give Bangladesh a platform.

Pakistan’s new-ball bowlers made early inroads, with Ali Raza dismissing both openers inside the first five overs.

Bangladesh made a cautious start and reached 41-2 after 13 overs, before Shahadat and Ankon rebuilt through patience and selective attacking shots. Ankon contributed 30, helping Shahadat settle before the partnership was broken.

Shahadat then found another useful ally in SM Meherob, with the pair adding a half-century for the sixth wicket. Meherob made 28 from 36 balls, but Pakistan struck twice in the 41st over when Hasan dismissed Meherob and Rubel in quick succession.

Sufyan Moqim was central to Pakistan’s recovery, finishing with 3-29 from his 10 overs and preventing Bangladesh from accelerating during the middle overs. Hasan took 2-30, while Raza also claimed two wickets.

Shahadat’s late surge, including a six to bring up his hundred in the final over, pushed Bangladesh beyond 230, but the total proved insufficient against Pakistan’s steady response.

The Shaheens’ disciplined chase ensured that Shahadat’s determined century went in vain and kept their title defence on course.

articles.title: Govt increases wheat import ceiling to curb price increases
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday decided to increase the wheat import ceiling by 150 per cent to 2.5 million tonnes to check continuously rising prices of wheat and wheat flour in the market.

The decision was taken at a hurriedly called and virtually conducted meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the Cabinet late at night, presided over by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The meeting was called in view of continuous increases in flour prices by 5-6pc on a weekly basis amid supply constraints.

The ECC “approved in principle the enhancement of the wheat import ceiling to up to 2.5 million metric tonnes (MMT) for Food Year 2026-27, to ensure adequate wheat availability, stabilise market prices and meet provincial requirements until the forthcoming harvesting season”, according to a statement issued after the meeting by the finance ministry.

The decision was taken after detailed consideration of a summary submitted by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research, seeking the enhancement of the previously approved wheat import ceiling from one million tonnes to 2.5 MMT. The decision will be placed before the federal cabinet for ratification.

The committee was informed that the provincial governments had initially assessed their wheat import requirements at 750,000 metric tonnes, which were then revised downward to 550,000 metric tonnes by the provinces themselves, according to the ministry.

“However, in view of the recent increase in wheat and flour prices and the need for enhanced releases from public stocks, the provinces have reassessed their requirements, raising the cumulative import demand to approximately 1.7 MMT,” the ministry statement said.

This includes 950,000 metric tonnes for Punjab, 450,000 metric tonnes for Sindh, subject to confirmation, and 300,000 metric tonnes for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Balochistan’s requirements are to be met through available Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation stocks.

The ECC agreed that enhancing the import ceiling to 2.5 MMT would provide enough flexibility to meet additional provincial requirements or shortfalls in available stocks, without requiring repeated approvals.

The actual quantities to be imported would be determined in accordance with confirmed provincial requirements and prevailing market conditions.

“The committee approved that the entire cost of imported wheat, including procurement, freight, insurance, transportation, port charges, taxes, duties and other associated expenses, would be borne by the respective provincial governments under the existing financial arrangements,” the ministry said, adding that the provinces would confirm their requirements in writing and ensure advance payments or appropriate banking arrangements in accordance with the agreed mechanism.

To facilitate the timely arrival and delivery of imported wheat, the ECC also approved priority berthing arrangements for wheat-carrying vessels at the relevant ports, in coordination with the maritime ministry and concerned port authorities, to minimise delays and additional costs, the statement said.

Regarding implementation of the arrangements, the committee agreed that while the Steering Committee headed by the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar would continue to exercise overall oversight of the wheat import programme, the food security ministry would be responsible for its day-to-day monitoring, implementation and execution.

It also agreed that any operational or implementation issues requiring intervention would be brought to the attention of the Prime Minister’s Office on a real-time basis for prompt resolution.

While the ECC approved the enhanced wheat import quantities, the finance minister emphasised the importance of timely assessment of wheat requirements, effective management of available stocks and close coordination between the federal and provincial governments to maintain stability in wheat supplies and prices.

Aurangzeb said that wheat availability and price stability needed to be addressed together, with particular focus on ensuring adequate releases from public stocks and responding promptly to changing market conditions.

“He stressed that a coordinated and forward-looking approach was essential to safeguarding consumers from inflationary pressures while ensuring the efficient use of national resources,” the statement added.

The minister stressed the government’s commitment to maintaining sufficient wheat supplies and protecting consumers from unjustified price increases. He emphasised that the decision was intended to provide flexibility to meet emerging requirements, while sending a “clear message” to the market regarding the government’s resolve to maintain price stability, the statement said.

Aurangzeb stressed the need for a collective and coordinated response by all concerned authorities to “discourage speculative practices, prevent market manipulation and ensure that the benefits of adequate wheat availability reach consumers”, calling for close monitoring and timely implementation of the decisions taken by the ECC.

Last month, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar expressed concern at the rising wheat prices and directed federal and provincial governments to take all necessary measures, including increasing market supply, to bring prices under control.

In October, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had set the indicative wheat support price for 2027 at Rs4,500 per maund (40kg), an increase of Rs1,000 from the rate fixed last year. The decision was aimed at supporting farmers, protecting their economic interests and boosting domestic wheat production.

articles.title: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary:
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

A meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) was held in the federal capital, where authorities announced a public holiday and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday was also announced in Rawalpindi.

The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries. Friday’s meeting lasted approximately two-and-a-half hours.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar thanked the participating officials.

He said that the SPDC comprised the foreign ministers, defence ministers, chiefs of defence forces and general staff of all three countries.

Dar said that he himself, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Asim Munir took part in the meeting.

He said that Saudi Arabia’s delegation comprised Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Chief of General Staff of the Saudi Armed Forces Gen Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili.

Meanwhile, Turkiye’s delegation consisted of Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu.

“I would like to take this opportunity to thank our distinguished guests for their presence here in Pakistan,” he said.

“The SPDC meeting reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security and stability,” he said.

Dar said that the three countries reiterated their commitment to the pact, including collective defence, mutual solidarity and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.

“The three sides also reviewed progress towards implementing the decisions taken at the previous meeting of the Makkah Alliance for Defence and expressed satisfaction at the pace of progress towards the establishment and operationalisation of the alliance secretariat in Saudi Arabia,” Dar added.

He said the SPDC agreed to continue consultations to enhance cooperation and coordination between the member states in areas of mutual interest, and to support efforts towards de-escalation of regional tensions and encourage peaceful dispute resolution.

The states condemned the “persistent and heinous” attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “collective resolve” to continue efforts in safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with the “collective defence provisions” in the pact, Dar said.

He further stated that the three countries also pledged to strengthen cooperation in defence industries, joint technological development, training and capacity building “with a view to enhancing the collective capabilities and cohesion of their armed forces in order to address mutual security concerns and contribute to peace and security in the region.”

Dar added that the meeting not only symbolised the bond of “longstanding friendship and solidarity” among the states but also “represents Pakistan’s continued efforts towards regional and international peace and security”.

“The meeting also shows Pakistan’s growing and robust diplomatic footprint at the international level,” he concluded.

The Foreign Office (FO) also issued a joint declaration after the meeting.

It also said on X that during the meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the alliance and underscored the importance of solidarity and close coordination in addressing shared security challenges.

“He emphasised the purely defensive nature of the alliance and its role in promoting lasting regional peace, security and prosperity,” it said.

In a post on X, Asif hailed the alliance, saying it positioned Pakistan on the global stage as a “strong, responsible, and reliable partner”. He said the joint statement issued after the meeting represented a “historic and far-sighted step” for Pakistan.

“For the first time, three major Muslim nations — Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye — have formalised and institutionalised their commitment to collective defence, mutual solidarity, and respect for sovereignty,” Asif said, adding that the alliance sent a “clear message that the Muslim world is uniting to ensure its own security, rather than looking to others”.

“The establishment of a secretariat elevates this alliance beyond mere rhetoric, placing it on a practical and permanent footing,” Asif wrote.

He further stated that the joint declaration had prioritised de-escalation of tensions via diplomacy, adding that it aligned with Pakistan’s “long-standing” position on peace.

On the condemnation of Houthi attacks, Asif wrote that supporting the security of Saudi Arabia was a commitment to the stability of the entire region. The three countries’ pledge to cooperate on the defence industry, Asif said, presented Pakistan with access to “advanced technology, greater defence self-reliance, and economic benefits”.

“By leveraging Turkiye’s expertise in the defence sector alongside Saudi Arabia’s resources, Pakistan can elevate its own defence capabilities to new heights,” Asif said.

He reiterated that the pact was aimed at regional peace, stability and collective security.

“At a time when power politics is on the rise globally, this alliance of Muslim nations serves as a symbol of hope, trust, and a shared future. Long live the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye!”

Dar, Fidan agree to maintain ‘close coordination’ under pact

On the sidelines of the meeting, Dar met with his Turkish counterpart, where the two expressed satisfaction at the “growing momentum” in bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, defence and energy, the FO said in a post on X.

The FO added that the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to each other on matters of mutual interest.

Dar and Fidan also agreed to “translate their strong political ties into tangible economic dividends and maintain close coordination under the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence to promote dialogue and de-escalation”.

Fidan, for his part, thanked Pakistan for “warm hospitality” and the country’s “active diplomacy”.

PM Shehbaz expresses satisfaction at meeting outcome: PMO

Following the conclusion of the meeting, the delegations from Saudi Arabia and Turkiye called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, during which the premier reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to the pact, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

The prime minister also welcomed the “strong unity and determination” displayed by the three countries in defending each other’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with the provisions in the agreement.

PM Shehbaz expressed satisfaction at the outcome of the SPDC meeting, the PMO added.

The premier also expressed “unwavering solidarity with the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reassuring full support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security”.

PM Shehbaz also held a dinner reception in honour of the participants at the PM House, PMO said.

The alliance

The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7. The pact provides that an armed attack on any one member will be considered an attack on all, obliging the other two to extend assistance through available means, including military support.

The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum.

A permanent secretariat has been established in Riyadh to coordinate its work, with Pakistan’s retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood appointed as its first secretary general for a three-year term. A working committee comprising officials from member countries is also functioning.

Turkiye’s ratification of the agreement has completed the accession process for all three member states, but the alliance’s institutional and operational framework remains at what Asif described as a “nascent stage”.

“Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” the defence minister said.

The alliance has yet to publicly define its doctrine, the composition of forces, command arrangements or procedures governing a collective military response.

An emergency SPDC meeting in Riyadh on Oct 5 had called for moving towards practical implementation of collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed forces and capabilities, subject to national laws.

Wider regional tensions

The alliance’s formation also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel.

While the three members share an interest in strengthening regional deterrence, their differing strategic priorities make it important to define the alliance’s scope without allowing it to become an instrument for wider military confrontation.

Asif declined to comment on how the alliance would respond to a direct Iranian attack on Saudi Arabia, but identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

A meeting in Tehran involving representatives of the three countries and Iranian officials, held on Pakistan’s initiative, reflected efforts to keep channels of communication open between the two sides.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and laid out a roadmap for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

However, the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy led principally by Qatar and Pakistan.

Asif said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

Recent Pakistani military deployments, including JF-17 aircraft, drones and air defence systems such as the HQ-9, were made under bilateral cooperation predating the alliance, a security source said, adding that these existing arrangements would now become part of the trilateral framework.

Meanwhile, Turkiye has stressed the defensive character of the agreement and remained cautious about involvement in combat operations in Yemen.

articles.title: President Zardari, PML-Q chief Shujaat discuss country's political situation
articles.summary:
President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday discussed the country’s political situation in a meeting with former prime minister and Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain.

In a statement, the Presidency said that President Zardari held the meeting with Shujaat at the latter’s residence in Lahore, where Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was also present.

“National affairs and the political situation were discussed during the meeting,” the statement said.

The president wished the PML-Q leader a speedy recovery, it added.

According to the statement, Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider, federal minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain, provincial minister Chaudhry Shafiq Hussain, former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim also attended the meeting.

The meeting comes in the wake of an ongoing debate over the creation of new provinces and the holding of a referendum, with President Zardari’s PPP opposing the move.

The debate was sparked by Naqvi’s July remarks, wherein he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Earlier this week, Naqvi also held a meeting with Shujaat, where the debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers was discussed.

During the meeting, Shujaat said the question of creating new provinces was directly linked to public convenience, good governance, administrative efficiency and the country’s future.

In the meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order, and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level.

Later that day, Naqvi met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, with whom he discussed the prevailing situation.

articles.title: Petrol price reduced by Re1 per litre, diesel price kept unchanged
articles.summary:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre while keeping the price of diesel unchanged, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs312 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs346 per litre until Nov 30 (Monday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively, as a result of price reductions made to both on Wednesday.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: 3 convicted of taking woman from UK to Pakistan, forcing her into marriage: police
articles.summary:
Police in the United Kingdom said on Friday that three people had been convicted of taking a young woman from the country to Pakistan and forcing her into marriage.

A statement issued by West Midlands Police noted that the woman was “particularly vulnerable” to exploitation as she did not have the capacity to consent to marriage.

“This conviction is understood to be the first in the UK which centres around a victim not being deemed to have capacity to consent to marriage,” police said.

“Mohammad Bashir, Khatoon Bi and Mobeen Akhtar, all from Birmingham, took advantage of a vulnerable woman in autumn 2024,” the statement said, adding that the police were alerted to the exploitation in early November of that year and immediate inquiries were carried out by their public protection unit.

According to police, the investigators learned that the involved parties were returning to the UK “within days”. Officers detained the three on Nov 7, 2024 at Birmingham Airport on suspicion of forced marriage.

“We also safeguarded the woman and, after speaking to her, we established she was unaware how she had been exploited,” the police said.

Deputy Senior Investigating Officer (DSIO) Mindy Mahil, one of the officers leading the investigation, said, “These three took advantage of a young woman, who was extremely vulnerable, and took her from Birmingham to Pakistan for marriage.

“It became clear to us immediately that the woman was being exploited, and that she did not have capacity to consent to a marriage.”

According to Mahil, the welfare of the woman was the priority throughout the sensitive inquiry.

“Forcing someone into marriage without their consent is abuse and control, and we will always seek to pursue offenders and support victims,” the DSIO said.

Following the trial at Birmingham Crown Court, Bashir, aged 55, Bi, 55, and Aktar, 38, were convicted of the offence and will be sentenced at a later date, the statement said.

articles.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 2 days after building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony
articles.summary:
KARACHI: A man buried under the rubble from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident occurred.

On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed. Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight.

Rescue 1122 said on Friday that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway.

Its spokesperson, Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris.

He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment.

The statement added that CM Murad had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the building collapse, warning that action would be taken against those found responsible for negligence.

Death toll rises to 8

In a separate statement, Rescue 1122 said the total number of bodies recovered from the rubble had reached eight.

The service’s spokesperson told Dawn that 11 people were still missing according to reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building.

He said it may not be advisable for the workers to provide a timeline for finishing the rescue and debris removal operation at this stage.

Khan said that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body.

He admitted that this pace of the rescue operation may be causing concern for the relatives of the missing persons, who were protesting the slowness of the operation.

Newly-appointed East Deputy Commissioner Kashif Nabi Khuhro, speaking to the media, denied that the pace of the rescue operation was slow. However, he pointed out that the collapsed building was situated in congested and narrow streets, where it was relatively difficult to move heavy machinery.

Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

articles.title: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
articles.summary:
Airline Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the long-haul budget carrier said on Friday, succumbing to soaring fuel costs wrought by the war on Iran.

Norse Atlantic ASA, which is listed on the Oslo Euronext Expand bourse, and other group companies are not part of the filing and are still attempting to stay in business, the company said in a statement.

Norse Atlantic, which launched in 2022, on Wednesday warned that its financial situation was “critical”, and the following day said it had suspended all flights and that the board could file for bankruptcy unless it urgently secured funding.

Earlier on Friday, Norse said its lessors had terminated their leasing contracts for all 12 aircraft in the carrier’s fleet, demanding that the planes be handed back, a claim contested by the company.

“The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the company and the group to find a solution,” Norse CEO Eivind Roald said in a statement.

“The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations,” Roald said.

The global aviation industry is suffering its worst crisis since the Covid-19 pandemic as the US-Iran conflict, which began at the end of February, disrupts operations, drives up fuel prices, and sends airlines’ costs skyrocketing.
