Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), a wet-lease partner of the airline, said earlier that it would shift its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester.

Norse in 2021 signed long-term leases for nine Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft from Ireland-based AerCap Holdings and six Dreamliners from Singapore-based BOC Aviation Ltd. It later returned three of the planes to AerCap.

In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aimed to meet rising demand.

By Damiete Braide

King Saheed Osupa, Obesere and K1 De Ultimate will headline the sixth edition of Fuji Vibrations, scheduled to hold on December 3, 2026, at Muri Okunola Park, Victoria Island, Lagos.

The annual concert, organised by FUJI: A Opera, will feature a mix of established Fuji stars and emerging artistes under the theme TIMELESS, celebrating the genre’s enduring appeal and evolution across generations.

Other established performers billed for the event include Atawewe, SK Sensation, Taye Currency and Shefiu Alao, while Musa Talent, Bukola OmoDaddy and Sanjay Rasheed Abefe will represent the emerging generation.

The organisers said the concert, which debuted in 2020, was designed to preserve, promote and reimagine Fuji music while introducing the genre to new audiences through live performances, exhibitions and cultural collaborations.

Fuji Vibrations has grown into a regular feature on Lagos’ December entertainment calendar, attracting music lovers and showcasing the influence of Fuji on Nigeria’s contemporary music landscape, particularly Afrobeats.

Speaking ahead of the event, founder of FUJI: A Opera, Bobo Omotayo, said the genre had continued to attract younger listeners without losing its traditional audience.

He noted that Fuji’s influence remained evident in contemporary Nigerian music, adding that its ability to evolve while retaining its identity underscored the significance of this year’s theme.

Beyond music, the concert will also spotlight Nigerian fashion and cultural expression through its annual aso-ebi tradition. The organisers announced purple as this year’s official colour, encouraging attendees to incorporate it into their outfits.

The event is supported by Supa Komando, ZURI and Regal Dry Gin, alongside the Lagos State Government, LASPARK, Events By Claud, AWCA, Dave Acoustics Production, Cantagali and DALA.

FUJI: A Opera is also collaborating with the Fuji Musicians Association of Nigeria (FUMAN) to honour the genre’s pioneers and create opportunities for upcoming performers.

The organisers said the concert would further reinforce Fuji’s cultural relevance while celebrating the musicians and audiences sustaining its legacy.

articles.title: ENIFF 2026 draws 1,040, bridges Enugu to global cinema, civic conversations
articles.summary:
By Bianca Iboma-Emefu

The Eastern Nigeria International Film Festival (ENIFF) has strengthened its position as a platform for global cinematic exchange and creative development in Southeast Nigeria, drawing 1,040 attendees to its seventh edition in Enugu, where films from 15 countries intersected with conversations on civic engagement, culture and the future of the creative industry.

The four-day festival, held from November 18 to 21 at Nile Cinemas, featured 57 selected films across eight categories under the theme, “Stories That Build Futures,” bringing together filmmakers, industry leaders, cultural institutions, students, audiences and international partners.

Beyond the screenings, ENIFF 2026 expanded its international footprint through its first collaboration with TV BRICS, while deepening engagements with the European Union and British Council on film, civic participation, professional development and the social impact of storytelling.

The TV BRICS Film Showcase introduced Enugu audiences to stories from different cultural backgrounds through My Sister Clara from Brazil, directed by Diego Alexandre; Charming Beijing, a China-Russia production directed by Ivan Zakharenko; and Translator from Ethiopia, directed by Zewdu Lingerh.

Festival Director and founder, Ujuaku Nwakalor-Akukwe, said the growing international participation reflected ENIFF’s ambition to position the festival as a platform through which audiences and filmmakers in Southeast Nigeria could engage with global narratives, institutions and opportunities.

“One of the things that stood out for us this year was the response of the audience to the diversity and quality of the films,” she said. “People came, stayed for the conversations and engaged with stories from different parts of the world. Before the festival ended, people were already asking about ENIFF 2027.”

The festival also sustained its third consecutive partnership with the European Union through European Union Day, themed “Your Vote Builds the Future,” which explored the intersection of storytelling, media, culture, technology and civic participation.

A panel discussion, “The Stories Behind the Choice,” moderated by filmmaker Ike Nnaebue, examined how narratives and lived experiences could shape public consciousness and influence civic choices.

The programme also featured a short film competition that attracted 20 entries, with six films shortlisted for screening. Ugwuona Caleb Uzodima, for *Pure Water*, and Kenneth Ekuma, for One Vote, emerged winners and received monetary prizes to support their creative development.

In furthering the cultural exchange, the festival screened the Spanish film También la Lluvia in collaboration with the Embassy of Spain in Nigeria. The embassy was represented by Eva Barta Martín, Administrative Officer and Cultural Adviser.

Industry engagement at the festival featured prominent voices from the film, media, cultural and institutional sectors, including Lucia Lecumberri, EU Policy Officer; Dr. Shaibu Husseini, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the National Film and Video Censors Board; Obi Asika, Director-General and CEO of the National Council for Arts and Culture; Donna McGowan, Country Director of British Council Nigeria and West Africa Cluster Lead; and Dr. Emeka Mba, Managing Director and CEO of Afia TV.

ENIFF 2026 also hosted Film Lab Africa II: Creative Hustle, in collaboration with the British Council, with the session themed “The Work Beyond the Work: Impact, Responsibility and Legacy in Film.”

The engagement focused on the realities of sustaining creative careers, exploring the responsibilities, opportunities and long-term impact filmmakers must consider beyond producing films.

According to Ujuaku, the festival was designed to extend its value beyond film screenings by creating opportunities for professional learning, networking, cultural exchange and growth.

“Film festivals should create possibilities beyond the days of the festival,” she said. “We want filmmakers to meet audiences, young creatives to encounter the industry, and international partners to discover the talent and stories coming out of this part of Nigeria.”

With attendance exceeding the capacity of its main screening hall and renewed audience interest in the next edition, the organisers said plans for ENIFF 2027 would focus on expanding the festival’s reach, partnerships and opportunities for filmmakers.

Supported by the Delegation of the European Union to Nigeria and ECOWAS, MTN Nigeria, British Council, Temple Productions, Iconic Steps UK, Tempio Media Advocacy Foundation and the Embassy of Spain in Nigeria, ENIFF continues to pursue its founding mission of promoting independent cinema, creative development and cultural exchange while connecting filmmakers in Southeast Nigeria to wider national and international opportunities.

Established in 2020, the festival has evolved into a platform for showcasing independent films, fostering creative conversations and strengthening the visibility of regional filmmakers within the broader global cinema landscape.

Editorial angle: This version leads with the festival’s audience reach and international positioning, while framing the civic dialogue, partnerships and industry development as evidence of ENIFF’s growing relevance rather than simply listing activities.

The post ENIFF 2026 draws 1,040, bridges Enugu to global cinema, civic conversations appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Attempted rape: Nigerian jailed in Ghana after using scissors to cut victim’s pant
articles.summary:
A 24-year-old Nigerian man, Anthony Ekpe, has been sentenced to one year imprisonment by a Ghanaian court for unlawful entry, indecent assault, and attempted rape.

The Volta North Regional Police Command made the disclosure in a Friday statement signed by Public Relations Officer (PRO), Volta North Region-Hohoe, Inspector Felix Kwao.

It said the conviction followed a formal complaint lodged with the Regional Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) on October 16, 2025, by the victim.

The statement reads, “Investigation established that, the convict forcibly entered the victim’s room at midnight, used a pair of scissors to cut her underwear, and attempted to sexually assault her.

“Police investigations further revealed that during the victim’s attempt to fight off the attack, a struggle ensued, leaving her with physical injuries before the convict fled the scene.

“On 29th October, 2025, the accused was arrested and arraigned before the Hohoe District Court same day where he was initially remanded into police custody to allow for further investigations. A duplicate docket was subsequently forwarded to the Office of the Attorney-General for study and advice.

“On 23rd October, 2026, Anthony Ekpe reappeared before the court, pleaded guilty on the charges and sentenced to one (1) year imprisonment and a fine of 200 penalty units.’

The Volta North Regional Police Command reiterated its commitment to protecting the public, particularly vulnerable persons, and ensuring that perpetrators of sexual violence are swiftly brought to justice.

articles.title: US blasts Tehran over ‘fabricated’ tanker, carrier, $2.5m Hormuz toll claims
articles.summary:
The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) has launched a strong rebuttal of claims by an Iranian Navy Commander, Admiral Shahram Irani, dismissing them as “fabricated lies” amid escalating tensions over maritime security in the Gulf.

In a Facebook post on Saturday, CENTCOM said the Iranian commander made multiple false claims concerning US forces over the past 24 hours, including that American troops stole two Iranian oil tankers, that Iran struck the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, and that Washington is charging ships $2.5 million to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Irani was quoted by Iran’s semi-official Fars News Agency on Friday as saying US forces had seized two Iranian oil tankers but Iranian personnel later boarded and recovered the vessels while American troops on board were asleep.

CENTCOM flatly rejected the account.

“FACT: Iran no longer has a navy. The entire situation the Iranian military commander described is another fabricated lie,” the command said.

On the second claim, that Iranian naval forces struck the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) on the first day of Operation Epic Fury, forcing US forces to seek evacuation support from regional countries, CENTCOM said the carrier strike group was never hit.

“The Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group was well defended and never struck by Iran as a result. In fact, the strike group completed a historically successful combat deployment to the Middle East and safely returned to the United States last month,” it said.

CENTCOM also denied the third claim that it is charging $2.5 million to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

“While U.S. forces and regional partners do control the Strait of Hormuz, there is no toll for passing ships. CENTCOM’s efforts have restored freedom of navigation through the international waterway. Thousands of ships and billions of crude oil barrels have transited the strait freely and safely under U.S. protection despite unwarranted Iranian aggression,” it said.

The war of words comes against the backdrop of the US and Israeli military campaign against Iran, originally launched on February 28, which prompted Iranian missile and drone attacks in the region and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy supplies.

CENTCOM said it is continuing to enforce a US blockade of Iranian ports, and separately announced on Friday that US forces had disabled the Palau-flagged vessel Pacific Archer after it allegedly violated the blockade.

The post US blasts Tehran over ‘fabricated’ tanker, carrier, $2.5m Hormuz toll claims appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Edo South marginalised in federal projects, ADC senatorial candidate, Iduoriyekemwen alleges
articles.summary:
By Ighomuaye Lucky, Benin

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate for Edo South Senatorial District, Hon. Matthew Iduoriyekemwen, has vowed to fight for increased federal presence and end what he described as the marginalisation of the district if elected to the Senate in 2027.

He lamented that Edo South, despite its historical significance, population and economic potential, had not enjoyed the level of federal government attention and representation required to drive its development.

Iduoriyekemwen made the remarks while addressing journalists at his residence in Benin City, where he outlined his legislative agenda and dismissed allegations that he had dragged the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, to court.

The former Majority Leader of the Edo State House of Assembly said his ambition was to provide effective representation for the seven local government areas in Edo South and attract federal projects, investments and other development opportunities to the district.

He identified security, industrialisation, infrastructure and economic empowerment as key areas he would prioritise, insisting that his eight years in the Edo State House of Assembly had given him the legislative experience and understanding required to represent the people effectively.

“I know what it means to represent your people in parliament and to agitate for their interests. I want to take the wishes and aspirations of Edo South to the centre and bring back what the people rightly deserve,” he said.

On the controversy surrounding his relationship with the Benin Palace, Iduoriyekemwen emphatically denied ever instituting legal proceedings against the revered monarch, describing the allegation as false and politically motivated.

He declared his unalloyed loyalty to the Oba of Benin, whom he described as his father and the father of every Benin person.

“I am a very loyal son to the palace. I am part of the Benin royal family. I revere the throne, and my loyalty is total and absolute. The Oba of Benin is the father of every Benin man,” he said.

He further alleged that political opponents were deploying artificial intelligence (AI) to manipulate audio recordings and circulate misleading information aimed at damaging his reputation ahead of the elections.

The ADC candidate also denied allegations of land grabbing, challenging anyone who accused him of unlawfully taking their property to come forward with evidence.

He, however, acknowledged being involved in legal disputes with some individuals over alleged defamation, explaining that the actions were necessary to protect his reputation.

“Certainly, I am not in court with the Oba’s palace. I have a reputation, which is more important to me than anything else,” he maintained.

He appealed to voters across Edo South to support his senatorial ambition, promising to champion the district’s interests at the National Assembly and make it a safer and more attractive destination for investors, businesses and residents.

The Ondo State Commissioner of Police, CP Johnson Ayo Babalola, has declared a firm stance against political thuggery, warning that the command would not tolerate any form of violence, intimidation or criminal activities before, during and after the 2027 general elections.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, DSP Abayomi Jimoh disclosed this in a statement.

According to the statement, CP Babalola gave the warning during a Saturday radio interview session on Adaba 88.9 FM, where he reaffirmed the command’s commitment to maintaining peace, law and order across Ondo State before, during and after the forthcoming general elections.

The CP cautioned individuals and groups who might be considering the use of violence to advance political interests, stressing that there would be no hiding place for political thugs or anyone bent on disrupting the peace of the state.

He particularly warned political parties, aspirants, candidates and their supporters against resorting to violence, intimidation, hate speech, inflammatory statements or other unlawful conducts during electioneering campaigns, rallies and political gatherings.

He urged members of the public, irrespective of their political affiliations, to shun violence and political intolerance, and instead embrace peaceful campaigns, mutual respect and issue-based political engagements capable of strengthening the democratic process.

CP Babalola further warned that anyone found in possession of illegal firearms or other prohibited weapons, or involved in activities inimical to public peace and security, would be treated as a criminal and dealt with in accordance with the law.

He disclosed that the command had already mapped out comprehensive security strategies and strengthened its operational preparedness to ensure adequate security coverage across the state.

He added that the command was equally putting necessary measures in place to guarantee a peaceful, safe and crime-free yuletide season, assuring residents and visitors of adequate security throughout the festive period.

Reaffirming his commitment to a whole-of-security approach, the CP emphasised that the command would continue to collaborate with relevant security agencies, stakeholders and members of the public to prevent threats, tackle criminality and sustain the prevailing peace in the state.

The CP reiterated that Ondo State must remain peaceful before, during and after the 2027 general elections, warning that political ambition must never be allowed to become a justification for violence or lawlessness.

He called on all stakeholders to support the police and other security agencies in the collective responsibility of securing the state.

articles.title: 2027: Ajadi unveils campaign council, announces ₦300m empowerment plans, shares vehicles to committee
articles.summary:
Ambassador Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Oyo Central, has inaugurated his campaign council, unveiled a ₦300 million empowerment programme and distributed vehicles to committee across the district ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Ajadi made the announcements on Friday during the inauguration of his senatorial campaign council at his campaign office in Moniya, Akinyele Local Government Area, Ibadan, Oyo State. The vehicles were handed over to committee across the senatorial district.

Addressing party leaders, candidates and campaign committee at the gathering, Ajadi reiterated his commitment to supporting party members and strengthening the APM’s political structures across Oyo Central. He said the proposed ₦300 million empowerment programme would be implemented before the 2027 general elections.

The senatorial candidate also called for unity among party members, urging them to support all APM candidates contesting at various levels of the forthcoming elections rather than divide their votes. He emphasised the importance of collective commitment and cooperation in achieving the party’s objectives.

Ajadi also commended Oyo State Governor, Engr. Seyi Makinde, for his leadership and contributions to the development of the state. He praised the governor’s approach to governance and expressed the hope that more well-meaning individuals would emerge to contribute to Oyo State’s progress through generosity and commitment to public service.

Earlier, the Director-General of the campaign council, Hon. Sanda Sikiru Oyedele, explained that the vehicles were provided to facilitate campaign activities and grassroots mobilisation across the respective local government areas. He urged the committee to ensure that the vehicles were used for legitimate purposes and in the collective interest of the party’s candidates.

Sanda also charged members of the campaign council to work harmoniously with the structures of other APM candidates, including the party’s women and youth coordinators, to strengthen mobilisation across the district.

In an interview with journalists, the Assistant Director-General representing the Ogbomoso zone, Hon. Seun Ojo, described the distribution of the vehicles to campaign committee as an unprecedented development in the political history of Oyo Central Senatorial District.

“Even when we have a Senate Leader from Oyo State, we have never experienced such a major political development,” he said.

The event attracted several political leaders and APM candidates, including Hon. Toheeb Adegoke, popularly known as ADLAT, the party’s House of Representatives candidate for Akinyele/Lagelu Federal Constituency; Hon. Lekan Abiola, its House of Assembly candidate for Akinyele State Constituency I; Hon. Waheed Akintayo, popularly known as Ilumoka, the candidate for Oluyole State Constituency; and Hon. Olalere Solomon, also known as Ere, the candidate for Akinyele State Constituency II.

Also present were Hon. Wole Akinleye, Chairman of Akinyele Local Government, and Hon. Simple, Vice Chairman of Egbeda Local Government.

The campaign council reaffirmed its commitment to expanding the party’s membership and strengthening its presence across Oyo Central Senatorial District as preparations intensify for the 2027 general elections.

articles.title: WWE star Bronson Reed dies at 38
articles.summary:
Wrestling star, Bronson Reed has died at the age of 38 due to “medical complications”.

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) announced his demise in a Friday statement.

Born in Adelaide, Australia on August 25, 1988, Reed’s real name was Jermaine Haley.

The statement reads, “WWE is devastated to announce that Jermaine Haley, also known as Bronson Reed, passed away earlier today at the age of 38 due to medical complications.

“Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague.”

WWE did not disclose the exact cause of death or specify whether it was related to injuries he sustained earlier this month.

Reed’s passing comes weeks after he reportedly suffered serious injuries during WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on November 7.

According to multiple reports, he suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney after being tossed offstage into tables during a brawl with Oba Femi, and stayed behind in Saudi Arabia for additional medical treatment.

The Australian wrestler began his career in 2007 on the Australian independent scene as Jonah Rock, before joining WWE for two stints from 2019 to 2021 and 2022 to 2026.

He is survived by his pregnant wife, Paige, and their daughter.

articles.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
articles.summary:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 21:13

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman expected to travel to the US next month for G-20 in first trip since start of war

This aerial photograph shows a view of the Riyadh skyline on 23 November 2026

Off

Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.

The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.

The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.

Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has tried to rally the US and regional states to his side. Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Syria have all sent or committed to delivering military support to Saudi Arabia, but with the exception of Syria - which has sent drone operators - the assistance is defensive.

The Crown Prince met US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, last week. MEE first reported the planned meeting, which was the third since fighting with the Houthis resumed in July.

The US, Saudi Arabia's top military supplier, however has not publicly committed additional support to the kingdom, although it has troops and advisers inside the country.

Iran tensions simmer

Semafor reported on Wednesday that Mohammed bin Salman will travel to the US next month for the G-20 summit in Miami. Diplomats have speculated for months whether the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia would leave the kingdom amid Houthi strikes and the chances of a new US-Israeli attack on Iran.

'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis

Read More »

Tensions between the US and Iran have been simmering for months, with the two sides exchanging blows in the Strait of Hormuz and at some land targets. The US has conducted strikes on Iran’s mainland while Tehran has responded with attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Iran said on Wednesday that an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a "restricted zone" in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Brent, the international oil benchmark, was up 2.5 percent on Wednesday, trading at $84 per barrel.

The Trump administration says that it is not interested in resuming the war on Iran for now, and instead wants to use economic means to collapse the government, mainly through a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran has been hit by debilitating inflation, although regional officials who have traveled to the capital have reported busy restaurants and a sense of calm. Fars said on Wednesday that a substantial shipment of dollar banknotes had entered Iran from a neighbouring country.

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year
articles.summary:
US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 18:44

The president's abrupt announcement came on the morning of the midterm elections earlier this month

Students carry placards depicting US President Donald Trump and Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu carrying guns, as they march during a general strike over rising living costs and military spending called by the CGIL trade union, in Milan, Italy, on 20 November 2026 (Claudia Greco/Reuters)

Off

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion earlier this month that he "won't be paying Israel" by the end of this year.

Huckabee, the former governor of Arkansas who is an evangelical pastor and a staunch Zionist - by his own description - said on Tuesday at a conference in Tel Aviv that he's "not certain that there will be a cessation on an abrupt basis by the end of this year". 

That's because Washington currently gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes.

In May, the Israeli defence ministry said that the two sides had begun formal talks to replace the current memorandum, with discussions focusing on joint investment in research, development and weapons production.

The suggested framework was to move the relationship from aid to a more reciprocal partnership. 

The Congressional Research Service, a non-partisan research body that advises the US Congress, further confirmed this in a June report that US and Israeli officials were discussing a possible shift after 2028 away from direct military aid and towards joint programmes.

Israel, a full-scale partner

In July, the Republican-controlled House of Representatives narrowly passed a $1.5 trillion budget for the US Department of War, and the bill included a controversial provision that would permanently integrate US and Israeli military tech advancements in a way that would - as Netanyahu put it - turn Israel from a foreign aid recipient to a full-scale partner. 

Future presidents would not be able to simply withdraw from such a project. 

Kushner says Israel is becoming a 'pariah' as his Board of Peace plans stall

Read More »

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is must-pass legislation, as it is needed to fund all of the Pentagon's operations in the year to come. The Senate will have to consider it soon.

But emboldened by the incoming Democratic majority in January, a dozen Democrats, led by Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, are seeking to remove the provisions related to Section 219, which establishes the "United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative".

The project would identify jointly developed or Israeli-origin technologies for potential integration into US systems; ensure collaborative research initiatives involving government, private sector and academic institutions in both countries protect "sensitive technology"; and ultimately align military efforts with the Department of War that include the Irregular Warfare Technical Support Directorate, the Defense Innovation Unit, the Missile Defense Agency and the United States Space Command, among others. 

Huckabee said at the Institute for National Security Studies conference on Tuesday that American lives are saved "every day" because "we pick up intelligence from our partners in Israel". 

Military ties continue

On 3 November, Trump said that his administration will not give its yearly military aid to Israel starting next year, because of a prior understanding he made with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Trump added that weapon sales and other forms of military cooperation would continue. 

Speaking on Fox News, the president said that the two had agreed months ago to end the military aid since Israel no longer needed it.

Britain must stand firm against Nusseibeh's UN candidacy

Read More »

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping,” Trump said.

“We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it,” he added.

Trump said Israel would be able to purchase weapons from the United States and other countries, suggesting that the change would affect the form of assistance rather than bring an end to military ties.

"They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world," he said.

The comments came as Republican lawmakers and establishment Democrats running for Congress - as well as hundreds of statewide races - faced growing electoral pressure over support for Israel ahead of the midterm elections.

And indeed, the so-called blue tsunami, led by an energised progressive Democratic movement that wants to curb US aid to Israel, washed over Capitol Hill and state legislatures, including several governorships.

articles.title: The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war
articles.summary:
The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war

Submitted by
MEE correspondent
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 14:23

A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away in the remote roof of the Sahara has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars

The Tibesti mountains run through northern Chad into southern Libya, and are home to the Tubu people (MEE)

Off

Deep inside the Tibesti mountains of northern Chad, in the central Sahara, the town of Miski sits surrounded by a succession of never-ending wadis. 

A couple of families live at the top of each of these valleys and in August, when the rainy season comes, the wadis become a river that washes through the mountains. When the rains go, the valleys become green and camels feed on them.

A remote volcanic range characterised by rugged, bare rock, rivers of lava and volcanoes that climb to 3,000 metres, the Tibesti, which runs through northern Chad across the border into southern Libya, is sometimes called the roof of the Sahara. 

These mountains are home to the Tubu, an indigenous community whose territory also includes a part of southern Libya, northern Niger and northwestern Sudan.

And the valleys that surround the town of Miski contain vast deposits of a precious metal that throughout human history has been prized almost above anything else: gold. 

The mountains, too, are filled with antimony, a toxic heavy metal that is putting the ecosystem of this indigenous community at severe risk and is also exported in great quantities. 

For decades, the gold that sits in this remote place has been one of the drivers of armed conflict between the Tubu and the Libyan, then Chadian states. 

Now, the Tubu find themselves caught up in a web of warfare and illicit trade that stretches out from Chad into Libya, Sudan and over the sea to the United Arab Emirates, from where arms and supplies are flown to proxy armies, militias and paramilitaries. 

On 14 October, armed clashes broke out in Miski.

The day after fighting began, the Chadian army’s general staff accused Miski’s self-defence committee - a local armed group descended from the Tubu institution of village guardianship - of breaking a peace agreement struck between them and the army last year by attacking the National Brigade for the Control of Mining Activities.

The army gave the Tubu group an ultimatum: lay down your arms at once or be treated as rebels. In response, the committee accused the brigade of firing first and of opening new mining fronts in grazing lands, in violation of the Bardai peace accord signed last year.

The gold ends up in Dubai…'yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti' 

- Tubu commander

One Tubu commander in Miski told Middle East Eye that last year Chad had exported over $1bn worth of gold and more than 15,000 tonnes of antimony, all sourced from the Tibesti mountains.

Almost all this gold ends up in the UAE, in the gold market of Dubai.

“And yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti,” the commander said. “We won’t let this continue.”

Since the armed clashes broke out in October, the Chadian army has moved considerable numbers of troops and armoured vehicles into the Tibesti.  

The situation on the ground, according to one Chadian army officer who spoke to MEE, is difficult for government troops. “We are fighting the mines and the mountains in Miski,” he said.

This fighting has not stopped: scores of people have died in the clashes and the Chadian army has conducted multiple drone strikes across the mountain range.

Weapons corridor

Miski’s uprising appears, on the surface, to be a local fight over gold - and in a large part, it is. 

But it is unfolding inside a region that has become one of the most consequential, least scrutinised arms corridors in Africa: a route that, according to United Nations investigators and extensive reporting from Middle East Eye, has carried weapons, fuel and fighters from the UAE through Libya and Chad to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan. 

How the UAE continued supporting Sudan's RSF through Haftar and Libya

Read More »

These weapons are part of a network of arms and mercenaries that spans swathes of north and central Africa, utilised not just in Sudan but by organised criminal groups and armed entities across the Sahel.   

Between October 2024 and the end of 2025, according to a UN Panel of Experts report, heavy cargo aircraft made 458 flights between military airports in the UAE or the Emirati base at Bosaso in the breakaway Somali region of Puntland and eastern Libya.  

Some 239 of these landed at Kufra, a town about 300km from the Sudan border that was transformed, in the months before the RSF took el-Fasher in October 2025, into a fortified logistics hub complete with new hangars and scheduled flights. 

Separately, as reported by MEE and confirmed by UN experts, the UAE was using Amdjarass, in eastern Chad, to land cargo planes.

Senior Egyptian army sources told MEE earlier this year that the Emiratis have a military operations room inside Amdjarass airport to coordinate with the RSF.

Just over 100km from the border with Darfur, the vast western region of Sudan controlled by the RSF, Amdjarass is a Zaghawa-dominated town that is the home region of Chad’s president, Mahamat Idriss Deby, and the site of a lavish state infrastructure programme that residents of Tibesti, 1,300km away and without a single paved road or a functioning hospital between them, have started to openly resent.

Abu Dhabi continues to deny supplying the Rapid Support Forces.

Haftar’s expanding footprint

In November 2025, Chad and the UAE-backed Haftar family’s Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), de facto commanded by Khalifa Haftar’s son Saddam, formed a joint border force covering roughly 1,050km of shared frontier.

The Haftars are not just in control of eastern Libya: leaked details of US adviser Massad Boulos’s plan to unify Libya propose Saddam Haftar as president of a government that would continue to be led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah. 

Chad’s government has two reasons to want this partnership, and they reinforce each other. 

One is logistical: Chad and Haftar can cement their relationship in the eastern Libyan corridor that carries Emirati arms to the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan. 

The other is that a joint border force hems in the Tubu, who have supplied the armed resistance to Mahamat Deby’s government and to Haftar’s forces alike. 

Jalel Harchaoui, an analyst focusing on Libya and political economy, told Middle East Eye that when the deal was initially struck, the Tubu were not part of the thinking.

The only connection in the remote area - Starlink (MEE)

“It was to ensure better security along the route between Chad and Libya, especially with the passage via Ma’tan as-Sarra in Libya down through Chad to Amdjarass and then on to Darfur,” he said.

This “security problem” included armed groups attacking the convoys headed to Darfur to supply the RSF, Harchaoui said. There was also the need to build further cooperation between Emirati allies who were not natural bedfellows.

“Saddam Haftar and Mahamat Deby don’t get along, so there was a need to please the UAE by doing a joint force. And the agreement was never that the joint force would be pushed to the west, it was really to cover the northeastern corner of Chad,” Harchaoui said.

That changed earlier this year, when Saddam Haftar “ran into trouble” with armed Tubu groups like the Southern Liberation Operations Room (Slor), which is led by Mohamed Wardougou, a Libyan Tubu, and often hides out in northern Niger.

Haftar asked Chad to move forces to the west, arguing correctly, according to Harchaoui, “that Wardougou’s activism served as a shot in the arm for the anti-Deby Chadian group Front for Change and Concord in Chad (Fact) in northern Niger”.

History of revolt

This move played into the Tubu’s long record of rising up against the central governments of Chad, going back to the country’s independence from France in 1960. 

Their most recent armed revolt, in April 2021, culminated in the death on the front line of President Idriss Deby Itno, who had decided at the age of 68 to command his forces in person. His son Mahamat succeeded him.

In Libya too, the Tubu rose against Muammar Gaddafi, and after his fall in 2011, they held sway over vast stretches of southern Libya until 2021, when Haftar’s forces pushed into the areas they had controlled. The containment effort carries a human cost well beyond Tibesti. 

In Libya, Tubu communities describe a steady tightening around their citizenship, with human rights researchers long having flagged discriminatory practices such as treating the Tubu as second-class citizens and stopping them from obtaining passports and IDs. 

'We do not want to be part of a bigger game… We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region'

- Tubu defence committee member

On 14 October, the same day gunfire broke out in Miski, Libya’s attorney general in Tripoli said he was prepared to strip the 28,000 families registered at Murzuq, in the Fezzan region of southwest Libya, of their Libyan nationality, citing alleged forgery. 

Because the overwhelming majority of Libya’s Tubu are registered through that one civil registry, the announcement reads as an existential threat: if carried through, most of Libya’s Tubu would become stateless.

On the border between Libya and Niger, Wardougou’s Slor group has fought a running battle with Haftar’s forces, using northern Niger as a rear base. The Slor’s declared aim is to remove Haftar’s men from southern Libya.

In July, photographs circulated online showing Chadian soldiers at Libya’s Wigh airbase, near the Nigerien border - evidence, the group’s leadership says, that Chad is fighting on Haftar’s behalf. 

On 20 October, the LAAF arrested a former Chadian minister and senior opposition figure, Hassan Soukaya, as he tried to cross from Libya into Niger, and handed him to the Chadian army.

Days later, Niger’s government publicly accused the Chadian military, with alleged French support, of carrying out a drone strike on 24 October near the Salvador Pass that killed two civilians. The attack was reportedly meant to target Slor positions in Libya, but hit Nigerien territory by accident.

The UAE-Israel desert axis

On 19 October, Israel’s second-ever ambassador to Chad landed in N’Djamena to present her credentials to Deby.

Since taking power after his father’s death in 2021, Deby has made a point of binding Chad ever closer to the UAE and Israel: diplomatic relations with Israel were restored in 2022, and the first Israeli ambassador in more than half a century - since Chad broke off ties in 1972 - was received shortly afterwards. Despite this, in November 2023, Chad recalled its ambassador from Israel, citing “the unprecedented tide of deadly violence” inside Gaza.  

Chadian alignment with the UAE is not only military. As previously reported by MEE, the Emiratis offered Deby “more than a billion dollars” to “flip Chad towards supporting the RSF” after the war in Sudan began, according to former CIA analyst Cameron Hudson.

Senior UAE and regional officials referred to ICC over role in Sudan atrocities

Read More »

That figure now looks like loose change. In May 2025, in Abu Dhabi, Chad unveiled Chad Connexion 2030, a $30bn national development strategy to remake the infrastructure of a landlocked country from the ground up.

The UAE was, by a wide margin, its most important bilateral underwriter, securing $20.5bn in total backing and signing 18 contracts of its own worth over $6.2bn. 

Among the headline projects: an 800-km Etihad rail line to Cameroon’s port of Douala, a 50 MWp solar plant by Global South Utilities, industrial zones, Abu Dhabi Ports logistics hubs, and critical-mineral exploration permits. 

The partnership has tightened Chad’s dependence on the UAE and has become, in effect, the economic lifeline of Deby’s administration. To the west, Chad is already at odds with its neighbour Niger, which has drawn closer to Algeria.

In late October, Algeria deployed troops to Niger, the first time it had done this outside its borders since 1973. The move came days after Niger’s military government survived a coup attempt on 28 August.

Algeria’s move into Niger, according to the retired Algerian diplomat Amar Belani, is designed to counter what he described as “a destabilisation strategy actively involving the United Arab Emirates, Morocco, Israel and certain French proxies.”

The current geopolitical shifts, Belani went on, together with all they entail by way of rivalry and intervention by foreign actors, mean that “new tools, such as a show of presence including at the military level, are no longer a taboo and will be utilised to draw and reinforce Algeria’s red lines.”

Borderlands unrest

What is forming, in other words, is not one war but two rival blocs assembling around unrest in the desert borderlands. 

Rape, ransom and execution: The road out of Sudan's el-Fasher

Read More »

On one side: the Sudanese Armed Forces (which receives backing from Egypt and Turkey), Niger, Algeria, and the Tubu in Libya and Chad. On the other: the RSF, the Haftars, the UAE, Ethiopia and the Chadian state, with the French leaning towards this camp.

And the local fights and the larger one are no longer separate. A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away deep in the remote mountains of Chad has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars, with a succession contest inside Libya’s eastern military establishment, and a Sahelian realignment redrawing alliances from Algiers to Khartoum. 

“We do not want to be part of a bigger game,” one member of the Tubu defence committee in Miski told MEE. “We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region.”

But whether it remains a local counter-insurgency or becomes the spark for something larger will depend less on what happens in the mountains of Tibesti than on decisions being made in Abu Dhabi, Benghazi and Paris.

Sahel

Oscar Rickett

Miski, Chad

articles.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes
articles.summary:
Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 15:56

Yemeni movement says the refinery attack was in retaliation to Saudi strikes, including one that killed at least 26 people earlier this week

This satellite image shows a large smoke cloud billowing over Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery on 25 November 2026 (Planet Labs PBC/Handout via Reuters)

Off

Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, on Wednesday, describing it as retaliation for repeated Saudi strikes that have killed scores of civilians.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that the refinery attack caused fires and came in retaliation for the "brutal Saudi aggression against our country, including its targeting of passenger buses and citizens' trucks in the Al-Maqatirah district of Lahij, as well as other crimes in the capital, Sanaa, and the governorates."

The attack in the district of Lahij earlier this week killed at least 26 people.

In a follow-up post on X, Saree responded to Saudi threats to retaliate against Yemen's civilian Hodeidah port, which Saudi Arabia has already bombed, by warning that all "enemy Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targets".

"We warn employees, workers and those near these ports to evacuate them immediately and stay away, and we call on all shipping companies to remove their ships from those ports immediately," the post added.

Ansar Allah, known as the Houthis, which controls the capital Sanaa and much of north and western Yemen, has been firing missiles at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July in a spillover from the Israeli-US war on Iran.

Riyadh broke the ceasefire, which also included Saudi Arabia, when it bombed Sanaa's international airport on 13 July.

Since then, the Saudi military has struggled to contain the Houthis and their ability to counter Saudi-backed forces in Yemen.

The ongoing attacks are wreaking havoc on the Saudi economy, oil infrastructure and the country's international image.

Airlines have cancelled international flights from the Saudi capital, Riyadh, while previous attacks on the country’s oil infrastructure have disrupted oil supplies.

The attacks have also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including football's AFC Asian Cup and the flagship Future Investment Initiative conference.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudis said that air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in the country's Eastern Province. They did not deny that the attack had struck the oil refinery there.

Who are Yemen's Houthis and what do they want?

Read More »

Satellite images reviewed by Reuters showed large swathes of thick black smoke around the refinery, covering an area spanning around 600 square kilometres.

The Houthis have previously targeted Ras Tanura, which has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, during the conflict.

The refinery forms part of a strategic complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast facing Iran, through which the country exported most of its oil before the Israel-US war on Iran started on 28 February.

Since then, Saudi Arabia has had to send some of its oil through Yanbu on the west coast along the Red Sea, which receives oil via the East-West pipeline and has also faced attacks.

Separately, Houthi spokesman Saree had also said the group had attacked Riyadh's financial district in three phases.

Saudi civil defence said a strike on Tuesday wounded 11 people at a tower in Riyadh’s financial district. The tallest building in the capital, the tower houses the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund. It was the second strike on the tower in less than a week.

The first, on 19 November, damaged the building but caused no injuries. Saudi civil defence posted an image on Tuesday of the landmark tower showing some damage about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact of last week's attack.

articles.title: Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution
articles.summary:
Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution

Submitted by
Katherine Hearst
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 13:02

Two letters signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups demand the 'immediate release' of defendants in Germany

The 'Ulm Five' from left to right: Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo (supplied)

Off

Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib are among dozens of politicians and legal organisations raising alarm over the prosecution and treatment of pro-Palestine activists in Germany.

Two letters issued on Wednesday, signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups from across the globe, condemned the treatment of five activists who have been held in pretrial detention for over 14 months.

Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo, who are from Germany, Spain, Ireland and the UK, were arrested on 8 September following an alleged break-in at the premises of Israeli arms firm Elbit Systems in the southwestern German city of Ulm.

Known as the “Ulm Five”, the group is accused of damaging the building's glass facade and smashing office equipment, including computers, screens and telephones.

In addition to charges of trespass and damage to property, the five are accused of "membership of a criminal organisation", namely Palestine Action Germany, under Section 129 of the German penal code.

The legislation is typically used to target organised crime networks and carries a potential sentence of up to five years in prison.

All the defendants have been held in prolonged pretrial detention, where they report facing restrictive conditions.

Under Section 129, suspects can be held for up to six months before trial, though lawyers say this period has now been significantly extended.

In their letter, the elected officials - including members of the German Bundestag, the European Parliament, the US Congress, the Irish Parliament and other legislatures across Europe and the Americas - called for the activists’ “immediate release”.

They further warned that the implications of their prosecution and treatment extend beyond the five defendants, forming “part of an international effort to discipline opposition to war and to place the interests of arms manufacturers above the rights of peoples and the obligations of international law”.

'Politically inconvenient facts'

Meanwhile, a separate letter signed by 33 legal groups - including the Center for Constitutional Rights, the Punjab Bar Council, European Democratic Lawyers, the American Association of Jurists, the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, the German Association of Democratic Lawyers - warned that the conduct of the trial could constitute a breach of German and international law.

In particular, the letter raises concerns about the courtroom’s security arrangements, which it said obstruct confidential communication between the defendants and their lawyers and could undermine the presumption of justice.

MEE previously reported that the trial, which began on 27 April, is taking place at a high security courtroom in the notorious Stammheim complex.

The defence team has repeatedly protested their clients’ treatment during proceedings, where the defendants are handcuffed and seated behind a glass barrier, preventing confidential communication with their lawyers.

The legal groups also challenged the court’s rejection of multiple applications by defence lawyers to hear expert witnesses. 

MEE previously reported that the court refused to hear weapons expert Dr Shir Hever and international law expert Isabel Feichtner, who were presented by the defence team to give evidence regarding Elbit Systems’ role in Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Germany’s obligations under international law.

The organisations further rejected the use of Section 129 against the defendants, insisting that “the prosecution of specific acts of property damage must not be conflated with the criminalisation of a political protest movement”.

"A criminal trial must establish the relevant facts impartially," they urged. "It must not exclude politically inconvenient facts merely because they concern the conduct of a powerful arms manufacturer or the actions of a state in an ongoing armed conflict".

articles.summary:
By Parisa Hafezi, Emily Giles and Melory Ghazi

DUBAI, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Iran's flogging of a female singer this week for offending public decency was a display of force by an embattled clerical elite straining to uphold public obedience it once took for granted, Iranian insiders say.

Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and four members of her production team received 74 lashes each on Monday for a livestreamed performance in a caravanserai near the holy Shi'ite Muslim city of Qom in which she had bare shoulders, no headscarf and male musicians, defying Iran's theocratic legal code.

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

articles.title: War, fear drive Sudanese writer Baraka Sakin's fiction
articles.summary:

The 63-year-old fled Sudan for Europe in 2012 and then returned, dreaming of an end to his forced exile.

But the war that erupted in 2023 and killed more than 200,000 people pushed him out again.

Still, he keeps writing.

articles.title: Freedom to Be: the UP100 Awards ceremony 2026
Freedom to Be: the UP100 Awards ceremony 2026
articles.summary:
On 26 November, the names of 100 Ukrainians who are shaping the future of this country were announced at the fourth UP100 Awards ceremony, held at the Museum of World War II in Kyiv. This year's theme was "Freedom to Be".

As ever, the winners were chosen in six categories: Defenders, Public Administration, Society, Business, Culture and Sport. Detailed profiles of all the winners can be found in this feature by Ukrainska Pravda.

The main sponsors of the event were Ajax Systems, Autostrada and DTEK. The title sponsor and awards partner of UP100: Freedom to Be was General Cherry. The premium sponsors of the ceremony were the pharmaceutical company Darnytsia, the jewellery studio AGA.TE, Apteka 9-1-1, Buntar Aerospace, CEO Club and La Famiglia Catering. The official supplier of alcoholic beverages for the UP100 event was Aznauri.

The evening opened with a gothic performance by the folk-fusion choir Horror, who blended folk motifs with a contemporary sound.

The evening opened with a performance from the Horror choir

Sevğil Musaieva, Editor-in-Chief of UP, then took to the stage to deliver the opening speech, which she admitted had not been easy to write this year. Sevğil reflected on the freedom to be a journalist and a Crimean Tatar and reminded the audience that Ukraine's future belongs to Ukrainians.

"When we first gathered in 2023, it was hard to imagine that the full-scale war would still be going on in 2026 – that at times it would be so difficult to plan your life even two weeks ahead," Sevğil said. "This year I've been thinking about what happens when extraordinary circumstances drag on for years. How do they change our understanding of what we have a right to expect, what we are allowed to want, and how much of our lives we are willing to put on hold until better times?"

UP Editor-in-Chief Sevğil Musaieva spoke about the freedom to be a journalist. Sevğil's outfit is by designer Lilia Litkovska

"Hence the theme of our gathering – Freedom to Be. I'll start with myself. The freedom to be a journalist means defending the freedom of the whole of society to know what is happening to it. The freedom to be an editor-in-chief also means protecting the people who are doing their jobs, and making decisions when the possible scenarios are very bad and very, very bad.

The freedom to be a Crimean Tatar. The last time I was in Crimea was summer 2014. Over the last twelve years, I have learned to say calmly that I can't return home for now. But sometimes I just really want to go home. And I know that many of you here in this room feel that longing too. I remember how ordinary it used to be to get on a train and go to see my family. There was so much freedom in the fact that I didn't even have to think of it as freedom.

We must determine the future of Ukraine ourselves. Over the years, I've been thinking more and more often about this word – 'ourselves'. It contains both the ability to act together and the right to see the future differently. And maybe it's precisely in those simple moments when we can listen to one another to the very end, even if we never reach agreement, that freedom is felt."

Sevğil Musaieva: "Thirty-five years of independence is a huge chunk of a human life. At the same time, for a country and in world history, it's a brief period. And it's painful to think that I may never see Ukraine as I dream of seeing it. But I deeply wish for other people after me – after us – to see that"

Sevğil then presented the traditional lapel pins to the families of warriors killed in combat: Oleksii Yukov, who since 2014 had worked tirelessly for Platsdarm, a search, recovery and repatriation group, bringing home the bodies of those whose lives were taken away by the war; Marat Mambetov, a MiG-29 pilot and flight commander in the Ghost of Kyiv brigade; and Andrii Horetskyi, an army aviation pilot. All the guests honoured the defenders' memory with a standing ovation.

"Our family has been hit by tragedy," said Oleksii Yukov's wife. "But when I was saying goodbye to my husband on the Maidan [Independence Square in Kyiv], I promised him that his mission would continue… I want to tell my husband that I am keeping the promise I made to him."

She also reminded the audience that her late husband had recovered the bodies not only of Ukrainian fighters, but Russian ones as well. They believed that these losses would help Russian mothers comprehend the full horror of the war.

One of the most poignant moments of the entire ceremony

Marat Mambetov's father spoke about the value of the Motherland and his pride in being a Crimean Tatar, as well as about his son, who gave his life for Ukraine.

"He was always one to step forward and volunteer. The last thing he said was: 'Dad, we have to go and kill those Russians. We will liberate our lands.' That's what he said to me."

The evening was hosted by actor and comedian Yevhen Yanovych, who joked that he could not have refused because he'd received a personal phone call from investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach himself.

Yevhen Yanovych was the host of the evening

Yevhen introduced the evening's first speaker – entrepreneur and former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov. In his speech, entitled "Freedom to Change the Rules", Mykhailo said he had always wanted to create something that people would appreciate – like the Diia app [Ukraine's e-governance app, which gives access to government services].

"Each of us has a different understanding of what freedom is," he said. "I come from Vasylivka, a small town which is currently occupied, from an ordinary family with no money or connections. Freedom is being able to imagine your future. Back then, I imagined that I could still achieve something without that money or those connections. That I would have an office without rooms – that's what I used to call an open-plan office – and now I have one. That a lot of people would work for me – last time I counted, it was 10,000."

Former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov spoke about the freedom to choose, using himself as an example

Mykhailo added that until a person has imagined their future, they will not know which direction to head in.

"At school I learned that you have to fight for freedom, because someone might decide they are physically stronger… Back then, the Yanukovych-appointed 'overseer' institution in Zaporizhzhia was restricting freedom of speech, preventing business from developing, and just stealing from the city. Back then, I was asked to leave university because they didn't like the protests I was organising. Fighting for freedom is always scary, unpleasant and super risky. It was scary, but I realised that fear passes, but your decisions stay with you forever."

Mykhailo Fedorov: "Putin will never understand Ukrainians – what freedom is, and what it means to fight for it. Remember those days: the queues at enlistment offices and Territorial Defence centres, the volunteers that would find anything that wasn't in the warehouses overnight. Farmers, IT specialists – everyone did what they could, and nobody waited to be ordered what to do"

In his speech, Mykhailo also mentioned his dismissal as defence minister in July this year.

"At a certain point I faced a choice: compromise or risk my post. I didn't compromise, and now I'm no longer in office. Do I regret it? Well, probably, yes. I never sought the position, but it gave me the opportunity to influence the course of the war. But if I'd agreed back then, I wouldn't be standing here today speaking to you about freedom. My mission hasn't changed – it's to defeat the Russians."

Next to take the stage, with a speech titled "The Fight for Justice", was another of this year's winners, Yeva "Yunha" Smyrnova, an FPV drone operator in the Rubizh Brigade who famously enlisted at the age of 18.

"Today, freedom costs us very dear," Yeva said. "Every day I'd have to remind people that I was just as much a combat unit as anyone else – that I could carry out combat missions on an equal footing with my brothers-in-arms. Every day, on our own initiative, we'd study FPV drones. When they arrived in our brigade, it wasn't long before we'd destroyed more than 250 enemy threats."

Yeva "Yunha" Smyrnova became a mother this year and lost her beloved husband

Yeva recently became a mother. Tragically, shortly before the birth of her son Yevhen, she learned that her husband, serviceman Danylo "Surfer" Smyrnov, had been killed in action.

"In war I gained no less. It was there that I met my love, my husband, Danylo 'Surfer' Smyrnov, who served in Defence Intelligence of Ukraine. We met at a very difficult time. We began planning our future together, realising that we didn't want only to fight, but also to have the opportunity to live this life.

Surfer and I had waited so long for this baby. We dreamed of being able to spend time away from the war. We had so many plans. I was in the ninth month of pregnancy when I learned that he had been killed during a mission. There are no words to describe what a person feels at such a moment. A month later I gave birth to our son... Yet motherhood has not taken away my understanding that the struggle continues. Now I have an even deeper understanding of what this daily struggle is for," Yeva admitted.

Next the host introduced Mykhailo Tkach, head of investigative journalism at UP, jokingly calling him his favourite "travel blogger" (Tkach was recently detained in Vienna). In his speech, titled "In Search of Truth", Mykhailo spoke about the challenges of his work.

"I would like to ask anyone who is suspected of espionage in Austria, or anyone who has been detained by special forces in Austria, to raise their hand. I couldn't help noticing that Ruslan Kravchenko isn't here with us today. He probably couldn't make it," he began – an allusion to the fugitive former prosecutor general that got a big laugh from the audience.

Mykhailo Tkach shared intriguing details about his work

Tkach announced that a court case is still ongoing with regard to an incident from five years ago when his team's cameraman was threatened with a knife for filming a meeting between politicians.

"And our lawyer called today and said we're probably going to lose. I asked: 'Why?' He replied: 'Those security guards proved in court that you were the ones who broke the rules, not them. You were filming them, and therefore you were in breach of the rules.' So we'll most likely lose this case.

Everything we go through in the course of our work is not in vain… A year ago we went to Vienna when Deputy Prime Minister [Oleksii] Chernyshov had gone there on an 'official trip'. We knew he was just running away, and we needed to ask him whether he was planning on coming back. That was when I felt the greatest resistance to our work. Various high-ranking officials started calling me in Vienna, saying: 'Mykhailo, the president said you have to be brought back to Ukraine,'" the journalist recalled.

Tkach's T-shirt is available in return for a donation to UP's investigative journalism department

Tkach went on: "In May 2026, we began writing that Andrii Yermak, who was head of the President's Office at the time, could be linked to the Midas case. After one article came out, Andrii Yermak called an acquaintance of mine and said: 'Tell him I haven't dealt with him yet.' I wasn't intimidated and replied: 'Tell him I haven't dealt with him yet either.' That remark was subsequently discussed at various meetings within law enforcement agencies."

This year's UP100 Awards

After Tkach's speech, the guests watched a video address by Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets, who led the humanitarian operation in Oleshky.

"Unfortunately, for all of us, since 2014, freedom has meant having to fight for it. In the literal sense of the word. To fight on the battlefield and on the front line of human rights protection. Freedom means constant survival and struggle by responsible people," Lubinets said.

Host Yevhen Yanovych also namechecked businessman Andrii Stavnitser, who secured investment from the family-owned Swiss company MSC in his container shipping business, TIS. MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company) is the world's largest container shipping company, accounting for more than 20% of global container fleet capacity.

"We also want to talk about Ukrainian business," Yevhen said. "The TIS team brought the deal to completion during the war, at a time when Russia continues to systematically attack Ukrainian ports. There are years of work and trust in the team behind this. It sends a signal to other investors that long-term partnerships with Ukrainian businesses can be built even during wartime. This deal was one of the reasons Andrii Stavnitser made this year's UP100 list in the Business category."

The first part of the evening ended with the formal announcement of the UP100 Award winners in the Defenders, Society and Culture categories, who were invited onto the stage to be presented with gifts and pose for a group photograph.

UP100 Freedom to Be Award winners

After the interval, guests enjoyed a musical performance by the Phil It creative collective, featuring vocals by Pylyp Koliadenko. The group performed several songs, including "Freedom", "Insomnia" and "Leave Something Behind".

Phil It provided a musical treat for the UP100 guests

"Thank you to everyone who is making our history, bringing about our victory, and fighting for our future," Pylyp said at the end of the performance.

Next to take to the stage was musician and service member Oleksandr Yarmak, another of this year's award winners.

"It's a great honour for me to receive such an award in such company. My personal transformation began in 2012-2013, when I was searching for my own path. Ukrainska Pravda has been my main source of information ever since," he said.

Musician and service member Oleksandr Yarmak

"We're going through a really hard autumn, and a hard winter lies ahead. We need to take action. Today I want to thank everyone present for being in Ukraine and for taking action. For standing firm. I'd like to raise the subject of culture. The war has shown me just how important culture is. I've met Cossacks who listened to Russian songs or watched Russian TV series. And I couldn't understand how that was possible.

We're risking our lives, yet people here are consuming their products. And these are such deep-rooted, fundamental processes. I've realised that culture is far more powerful than weapons. It can conquer territory, entire nations, and people's minds. It can shape patterns that go on to define an entire generation."

General Cherry was the event's title sponsor

The next speaker was Andrii Toiunda, head of the line repair and maintenance centre at DTEK Kyiv Electric Grids, who spoke about the challenging nature of his work and reminded everyone that he and his colleagues work tirelessly to restore electricity to people's homes.

"Sometimes after work there isn't even time to go home, so we rest at work... After Irpin was liberated from Russian occupation, we went in to repair the infrastructure, but there was nothing left to repair. We had to rebuild everything from scratch... I would like you to learn about some people whose work often goes unnoticed – miners. They go down into the mines to extract coal while the enemy is attacking the energy infrastructure. The power goes out, people are trapped underground, there's no lighting, the ventilation stops working and pumping out water becomes difficult. It's a titanic effort," Andrii stressed.

Andrii Toiunda: "The enemy reduces power stations to zero. It did this 11 times last year and it's done it 74 times since the war began. And these were the people who repaired those power stations. You want your power line repaired, and meanwhile, we are doing everything possible and impossible to get electricity back into your homes"

Yevhen Yanovych then invited Sevğil Musaieva to preside over a charity auction, with all proceeds going to Serhii Sternenko's foundation.

Lot one, part of a destroyed church in the village of Lukashivka in Chernihiv Oblast, was bought by Yanovych himself for US$10,000.

The first auction lot

Lot two was a print entitled "Svarga 2023" by artist Dmytro Krishovsky, together with a traditional Ukrainian ducat pendant featuring the Cossack Mamai. This lot sold for UAH 250,000 (about US$5,550).

The second lot

The final lot was a piece of cardboard belonging to Oleksandr Abakumov, head of a detectives unit at the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU), that reads "Corrupt Carthage must be destroyed". It was purchased by businessman Artem Borodatiuk for UAH 250,000.

Artem Borodatiuk and Oleksandr Abakumov

Oleksandr Abakumov also addressed the audience, thanking Ukraine's defenders and all the Ukrainians who have supported NABU and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO).

"We've seen a lot in the 11 years of NABU and SAPO's existence. We've been investigated in criminal cases against us; we've been beaten, detained and charged. But none of this has stopped us. Today we see the vast resources of the Security Service of Ukraine and the people whose criminal activities we were investigating being used against us. They are trying to put pressure on me and our detectives. But it didn't work then and it won't work now. If someone has committed a crime, it must be investigated."

Yevhen Yanovych with the item he purchased in support of Serhii Sternenko's foundation

Next up was a video address from another award winner, Vladyslav Heraskevych, the skeleton racer who was disqualified from the Winter Olympics for wearing a helmet that commemorated the Ukrainian athletes who have been killed due to Russia's aggression against Ukraine.

"Freedom is no longer such a simple thing today," Heraskevych said. "It means being able to speak your own language, knowing that your family and loved ones are safe, being able to do what you love. Right now our country is having to fight for its freedom every single day. We don't deserve this; it is a grave injustice. But I believe that freedom must and will prevail."

Then Artistka Chuprynenko (Mariia Chuprynenko) gave a moving performance based on a work by writer Artem Chapeye. Chuprynenko began by telling the story of a family who lost their home because of the war in an emotionally charged, unaccompanied monologue before incorporating guitar music into her performance.

Artistka Chuprynenko was one of this year's UP100 Award winners and also performed at the ceremony

Another poignant moment from the event

This was followed by a conversation between Iryna Chechotkina, co-founder of online retail giant Rozetka, and Sevğil Musaieva.

"We choose to live," Iryna said. "I look at people, at Ukrainians, and realise that each of them is choosing their own freedom. Ukraine is my home and always has been. For me, choosing Ukraine means doing my job. I now travel around Ukraine a great deal, supporting our employees, and I see how they continue to build businesses in different cities."

Iryna Chechotkina and Sevğil Musaieva

The evening closed with the announcement of the remaining 50 winners of the UP100 Freedom to Be Award in the Public Administration, Business and Sport categories. They were also invited onto the stage and presented with gifts.

Last year, the heads of SAPO and NABU spoke at the UP100 Awards ceremony – you can read more about it here.

The number injured later rose to three. Another woman sustained cuts and lacerations to her hands from broken glass, and a man suffered a closed head injury.

All three were taken to hospital.

A fire also broke out on the premises of garages in Bila Tserkva, damaging six garages. The blast wave shattered windows in two apartment buildings.

Search and rescue operations at the site of a Russian attack on a business in Nizhyn, Chernihiv Oblast, on 27 November have been completed. The death toll has risen to seven, and another seven people have been injured.

Source: State Emergency Service of Ukraine

Details: Rescue workers managed to pull one person from under the rubble.

A total of 55 State Emergency Service rescue workers and 14 emergency vehicles were involved in dealing with the aftermath of the attack. Two sniffer dogs and their handlers also took part in the operation.
